Saeima ir pieņēmusi un Valsts prezidents izsludina šādu likumu:

Krimināllikums

VISPĀRĪGĀ DAĻA

I nodaļa Vispārīgie noteikumi

### 1. pants. Kriminālatbildības pamats

(1)	Pie kriminālatbildības saucama un sodāma tikai tāda persona, kura ir vainīga noziedzīga nodarījuma izdarīšanā, tas ir, kura ar nodomu (tīši) vai aiz neuzmanības izdarījusi šajā likumā paredzētu nodarījumu, kam ir visas noziedzīga nodarījuma sastāva pazīmes.

(2)	Atzīt par vainīgu noziedzīga nodarījuma izdarīšanā un uzlikt kriminālsodu var ar tiesas spriedumu un saskaņā ar likumu.

(3)	Likumā noteiktajos gadījumos personu atzīst par vainīgu noziedzīga nodarījuma izdarīšanā un sodu nosaka arī prokurors, sastādot priekšrakstu par sodu.

(4)	Nodarījumu nevar atzīt par noziedzīgu, likumu piemērojot pēc analoģijas.

(5)	Nevienu nedrīkst no jauna tiesāt vai sodīt par nodarījumu, par kuru viņš jau ticis attaisnots vai sodīts ar likumā noteiktajā kārtībā pieņemtu un spēkā stājušos nolēmumu krimināllietā vai administratīvā pārkāpuma lietā. Minētais neizslēdz atkārtotu lietas izskatīšanu saskaņā ar likumu, ja ir konstatēti jaunatklāti apstākļi vai ja iepriekšējā procesā pieļauts būtisks materiālo vai procesuālo likuma normu pārkāpums, kas varēja ietekmēt lietas iznākumu.
(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 28.09.2005., 13.12.2012. un 15.05.2014. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 14.06.2014.)

The Saeima has adopted and the President of State proclaims the following law:

Criminal Law

GENERAL PART

I Chapter General Provisions

### Section 1. Basis for Criminal Liability

(1)	Only a person who is guilty of committing a criminal offence may be held criminally liable and punished, that is, a person who intentionally or through negligence has committed an act provided for in this Law which has all the elements of a criminal offence.

(2)	A person may be found guilty of committing a criminal offence and a criminal punishment may be imposed by a court judgment and in accordance with law.

(3)	In cases provided for by law, a person is also found guilty of committing a criminal offence and a punishment is imposed by a prosecutor by issuing a penal order.

(4)	An act may not be recognised as criminal by applying the law by analogy.

(5)	No one may be tried or punished again for an act for which he or she has already been acquitted or punished by a decision in a criminal case or administrative offence case adopted in accordance with the procedure provided for by law and which has entered into force. The aforementioned does not preclude repeated examination of a case in accordance with law if newly discovered circumstances have been established or if a material breach of substantive or procedural law has been committed in the previous proceedings which could have affected the outcome of the case.
(With amendments made by the laws of 28.09.2005., 13.12.2012. and 15.05.2014., which enter into force on 14.06.2014.)

### 2. pants. Krimināllikuma spēks Latvijas teritorijā

(1)	Persona, kas izdarījusi noziedzīgu nodarījumu Latvijas teritorijā, atbild saskaņā ar šo likumu.

(2)	Ja noziedzīgu nodarījumu Latvijas teritorijā izdarījis ārvalstu diplomātiskais pārstāvis vai cita persona, kura saskaņā ar spēkā esošajiem likumiem vai Latvijas Republikai saistošiem starptautiskajiem līgumiem nav pakļauta Latvijas Republikas jurisdikcijai, jautājums par šīs personas saukšanu pie kriminālatbildības izlemjams diplomātiskā ceļā vai saskaņā ar valstu savstarpējo vienošanos.

### 3. pants

Krimināllikuma spēks uz gaisakuģiem, jūras un upju kuģiem ārpus Latvijas teritorijas

Persona, kas noziedzīgu nodarījumu izdarījusi ārpus Latvijas teritorijas, atrodoties uz gaisakuģa, jūras vai upju kuģa vai cita peldoša līdzekļa, ja šis līdzeklis reģistrēts Latvijas Republikā un ja Latvijas Republikai saistošos starptautiskajos līgumos nav noteikts citādi, saucama pie atbildības saskaņā ar šo likumu.

### 4. pants. Krimināllikuma spēks ārpus Latvijas teritorijas

(1)	Latvijas pilsoņi, nepilsoņi vai ārzemnieki, kuriem ir pastāvīgās uzturēšanās atļauja Latvijas Republikā, par citas valsts teritorijā vai ārpus jebkuras valsts teritorijas izdarītu nodarījumu neatkarīgi no tā, vai tas izdarīšanas vietā atzīts par noziedzīgu un sodāmu, saucami pie atbildības Latvijas teritorijā saskaņā ar šo likumu.

(11) Par citas valsts teritorijā vai ārpus jebkuras valsts teritorijas izdarītu nodarījumu neatkarīgi no tā, vai tas izdarīšanas vietā atzīts par noziedzīgu un sodāmu, ja to izdarījusi fiziskā persona Latvijas Republikā reģistrētas juridiskās personas interesēs, labā vai juridiskās personas nepienācīgas pārraudzības vai kontroles rezultātā, juridiskajai personai var piemērot šajā likumā paredzētos piespiedu ietekmēšanas līdzekļus.

(2)	Latvijas Republikas karavīri, kuri izvietoti ārpus Latvijas teritorijas, par noziedzīgiem nodarījumiem saucami pie atbildības saskaņā ar šo likumu, ja Latvijas Republikai saistošos starptautiskajos līgumos nav noteikts citādi.

### 2. Section. Force of the Criminal Law in the Territory of Latvia

(1)	A person who has committed a criminal offence in the territory of Latvia shall be held liable in accordance with this Law.

(2)	If a criminal offence in the territory of Latvia has been committed by a foreign diplomatic representative or another person who, in accordance with laws in force or international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia, is not subject to the jurisdiction of the Republic of Latvia, the question of bringing this person to criminal liability shall be decided through diplomatic channels or in accordance with mutual agreement between states.

### 3. Section

Force of the Criminal Law on Aircraft, Sea and River Vessels Outside the Territory of Latvia

A person who has committed a criminal offence outside the territory of Latvia while on board an aircraft, sea or river vessel or other floating craft, if this craft is registered in the Republic of Latvia and if international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia do not provide otherwise, shall be brought to liability in accordance with this Law.

### 4. Section. Force of the Criminal Law Outside the Territory of Latvia

(1)	Citizens of Latvia, non-citizens or foreigners who have a permanent residence permit in the Republic of Latvia, for an offence committed in the territory of another state or outside the territory of any state, regardless of whether it is recognised as criminal and punishable at the place of commission, shall be brought to liability in the territory of Latvia in accordance with this Law.

(11) For an offence committed in the territory of another state or outside the territory of any state, regardless of whether it is recognised as criminal and punishable at the place of commission, if it has been committed by a natural person in the interests of, for the benefit of, or as a result of inadequate supervision or control of a legal person registered in the Republic of Latvia, coercive measures provided for in this Law may be applied to the legal person.

(2)	Military personnel of the Republic of Latvia who are deployed outside the territory of Latvia shall be brought to liability for criminal offences in accordance with this Law, unless international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia provide otherwise.

(3)	Foreigners who do not have a permanent residence permit in the Republic of Latvia and who have committed serious or particularly serious crimes in the territory of another state directed against the interests of the Republic of Latvia or its inhabitants, regardless of the laws of the state in whose territory the crime was committed, shall be brought to criminal liability in accordance with this Law if they have not been brought to criminal liability or brought to trial in accordance with the laws of the state where the crime was committed.

(4)	Foreigners who do not have a permanent residence permit in the Republic of Latvia and who have committed a criminal offence in the territory of another state or outside the territory of any state, regardless of the laws of the state where the offence was committed, shall be brought to liability in accordance with this Law in cases provided for in international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia, if they have not been brought to criminal liability or brought to trial in the territory of another state for this offence.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 17.10.2002., 16.12.2004., 21.05.2009., 21.10.2010. and 25.09.2014., which
enter into force on 29.10.2014.)

### 5. Section. Force of the Criminal Law in Time

(1)	The criminality and punishability of an offence (act or omission) shall be determined by the law that was in force at the time of the commission of this offence.

(2)	A law that recognises an offence as non-punishable, mitigates punishment or is otherwise favourable to a person, unless the respective law provides otherwise, shall have retroactive effect, namely, it shall apply to offences committed before the entry into force of the respective law, as well as to a person who is serving a punishment or has served a punishment but for whom punishability has been retained.

(3)	A law that recognises an offence as punishable, increases punishment or is otherwise unfavourable to a person shall not have retroactive effect.

(4)	A person who has committed a crime against humanity, a crime against peace, a war crime and has participated in genocide shall be punishable regardless of the time of commission of these crimes.

II	Chapter Criminal Offence

### 6. Section. Concept of a Criminal Offence

(1)	A criminal offence shall be recognised as a harmful offence (act or omission) committed with intent (intentionally) or through negligence, which is provided for in this Law and for the commission of which a criminal punishment is threatened.

(2)	An offence (act or omission) that has the elements of an offence provided for in this Law but has been committed in circumstances that exclude criminal liability shall not be recognised as criminal.
(With amendments made by the Law of 13.12.2012., which enters into force on 01.04.2013.)

### 7. Section. Classification of Criminal Offences

(1)	According to the nature and harmfulness of the threat to the interests of a person or society, criminal offences shall be divided into criminal violations and crimes. Crimes shall be divided as follows: less serious crimes, serious crimes and particularly serious crimes.

(2)	A criminal violation is an offence for which this Law provides deprivation of liberty for a period from fifteen days but not longer than three months (short-term deprivation of liberty), or a lighter type of punishment.

(3)	A less serious crime is an intentional offence for which this Law provides deprivation of liberty for a period longer than three months but not longer than three years, as well as an offence committed through negligence for which this Law provides deprivation of liberty for a period not longer than eight years.

(4)	A serious crime is an intentional offence for which this Law provides deprivation of liberty for a period longer than three years but not longer than eight years, as well as an offence committed through negligence for which this Law provides deprivation of liberty for a period longer than eight years.

(5)	A particularly serious crime is an intentional offence for which this Law provides deprivation of liberty for a period longer than eight years, or life imprisonment.

(6)	If for a crime this Law provides deprivation of liberty for a period not longer than five years, then for the respective crime it shall also provide a lighter type of punishment.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 21.05.2009., 01.12.2011., 13.12.2012. and 17.12.2020., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 8. Section. Forms of Guilt

(1)	Only a person who has committed it with intent (intentionally) or through negligence shall be recognised as guilty of a criminal offence.

(2)	When determining the form of guilt of a person who has committed a criminal offence, the mental attitude of this person towards the objective elements of the criminal offence must be established.

### 9. Section. Commission of a Criminal Offence with Intent (Intentionally)

(1)	A criminal offence shall be recognised as committed with intent (intentionally) if the person has committed it with direct or indirect intent.

(2)	A criminal offence shall be recognised as committed with direct intent if the person was aware of the harmfulness of their act or omission and consciously performed or permitted it, or was aware of the harmfulness of their act or omission, foresaw the harmful consequences of the offence and desired their occurrence.

(3)	A criminal offence shall be recognised as committed with indirect intent if the person was aware of the harmfulness of their act or omission, foresaw the harmful consequences of the offence and, although they did not desire these consequences, nevertheless consciously permitted their occurrence.
(In the wording of the Law of 13.12.2012., which enters into force on 01.04.2013.)

### 10. pants. Commission of a Criminal Offence through Negligence

(1)	A criminal offence shall be deemed to have been committed through negligence if a person has committed it through criminal overconfidence or criminal carelessness.

(2)	A criminal offence shall be deemed to have been committed through criminal overconfidence if a person has foreseen the possibility of the occurrence of harmful consequences of his or her action or inaction, but has frivolously relied on being able to prevent them.

(3)	A criminal offence shall be deemed to have been committed through criminal carelessness if a person has not foreseen the possibility of the occurrence of harmful consequences of his or her action or inaction, although according to the specific circumstances of the offence he or she should have and could have foreseen the said harmful consequences.

(4)	An offence provided for in this Law shall not be criminally punishable if a person did not foresee, should not have and could not have foreseen the possibility of the occurrence of harmful consequences of his or her action or inaction.

### 11. pants. Age at Which Criminal Liability Arises

A natural person who has reached the age of fourteen years by the day of commission of a criminal offence may be held criminally liable. A minor, that is, a person who has not reached the age of fourteen years, may not be held criminally liable.

### 12. pants. Liability of a Natural Person in a Case of a Legal Person

For a criminal offence committed by a natural person in the interests of a private law legal person, for the benefit of such person or as a result of its inadequate supervision or control, the respective natural person shall be held criminally liable, and coercive measures provided for in this Law may be applied to the legal person.
(14.03.2013. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.04.2013.)

### 13. pants. Insanity

(1)	A person who at the time of commission of an offence was in a state of insanity, that is, due to mental disorders or mental retardation was unable to understand his or her actions or to control them, may not be held criminally liable.

(2)	The court may apply coercive measures of a medical nature provided for in this Law to a person who has been recognised as insane.
(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 20.03.2014. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 03.04.2014.)

### 14. pants. Diminished Capacity

(1)	If at the time of commission of a criminal offence a person, due to mental disorders or mental retardation, was not fully capable of understanding his or her actions or controlling them, that is, was in a state of diminished capacity, the court, depending on the specific circumstances of the offence, may mitigate the penalty to be imposed or release this person from punishment.

(2)	The court shall apply coercive measures of a medical nature provided for in this Law to a person who has been recognised as having diminished capacity.

### 15. pants. Completed and Uncompleted Criminal Offence

(1)	A criminal offence shall be deemed completed if it has all the elements of a criminal offence provided for in this Law.

(2)	Preparation for a crime and an attempt to commit a crime shall be an uncompleted criminal offence.

(3)	Preparation for a crime shall be deemed to be the search for or adaptation of means or instruments or other intentional creation of favourable circumstances for the commission of an intentional crime, if, moreover, it has not been continued due to reasons independent of the will of the guilty person. Criminal liability shall arise only for preparation for serious or particularly serious crimes.

(4)	An attempt to commit a crime shall be deemed to be a deliberate action (inaction) directly aimed at its intentional commission, if

the crime has not been completed due to reasons independent of the will of the guilty person.

(5)	Liability for preparation for a crime or an attempt to commit a crime shall arise in accordance with the same Article of this Law that provides for liability for the specific offence.

(6)	A person may not be held criminally liable for an attempt to commit a misdemeanour.

### 16. pants. Voluntary Renunciation

(1)	Voluntary renunciation of the commission of a criminal offence shall be the complete cessation by a person of a criminal offence that has been commenced, of his or her own will, while being aware that there is a possibility to complete the criminal offence.

(2)	A person who has voluntarily renounced the commission of a criminal offence may not be held criminally liable. Such person shall be liable only if the offence actually committed by him or her contains the elements of another criminal offence.

### 17. pants. Perpetrator of a Criminal Offence

A person who has directly committed a criminal offence himself or herself or has used another person in its commission who, in accordance with the provisions of this Law, may not be held criminally liable, shall be deemed to be the perpetrator of a criminal offence.

### 18. pants. Participation of Several Persons in a Criminal Offence

Joint deliberate participation of two or more persons in the commission of an intentional criminal offence shall be co-perpetration or complicity.

### 19. pants. Co-perpetration

Co-perpetration shall be deemed to be a deliberate criminal action by which two or more persons (that is, a group) have directly committed an intentional criminal offence jointly, being aware of it. Each of these persons shall be a participant (co-perpetrator) in the criminal offence.

### 20. pants. Complicity

(1)	Complicity shall be deemed to be a deliberate action or inaction by which a person (accomplice) has participated jointly with another person (perpetrator) in the commission of an intentional criminal offence, but has not himself or herself been its direct perpetrator. Accomplices to a criminal offence shall be organisers, instigators, aiders.

(2)	An organiser shall be deemed to be a person who has organised or directed the commission of a criminal offence.

(3)	An instigator shall be deemed to be a person who has induced another person to commit a criminal offence.

(4)	An aider shall be deemed to be a person who has deliberately facilitated the commission of a criminal offence by giving advice, instructions, means or removing obstacles to its commission, as well as a person who has promised in advance to conceal the perpetrator of a criminal offence or an accomplice, the instruments and means of commission of a criminal offence, the traces of a criminal offence or objects obtained in a criminal manner, or has promised in advance to acquire or dispose of such objects.

(5)	An accomplice to criminal offences shall be held liable in accordance with the same Article of this Law that provides for the liability of the perpetrator.

(6)	Individual elements of a criminal offence relating to the perpetrator of a criminal offence or an accomplice shall not affect the liability of other co-perpetrators or accomplices.

(7)	If an accomplice was not aware of any of the criminal offences committed by the perpetrator and other accomplices, he or she may not be held criminally liable for them.

(8)	If the perpetrator has not completed the crime due to reasons independent of his or her will, the accomplices shall be liable for complicity in an attempt to commit the respective crime. If the perpetrator has not commenced the commission of the crime, the accomplices shall be liable for preparation for the respective crime.

(9)	Voluntary renunciation by an organiser and an instigator of the completion of a criminal offence shall be deemed to be such only in cases where they have done everything possible in a timely manner to prevent the commission of the criminal offence intended with their complicity, and this offence has not been committed. ### 21. pants. Organised Group

(1)	An organised group shall be an association formed by more than two persons, which has been created for the purpose of jointly committing one or more crimes and the members of which have divided duties in accordance with a prior agreement.

(2)	Liability for the commission of a crime in an organised group shall arise for a person in the cases provided for in this Law for the formation and direction of a group, participation in the preparation of a serious or particularly serious crime or the commission of a crime, regardless of the person's role in the jointly committed offence.

### 22. Section. Previously Unpromised Concealment and Failure to Report

(1) Previously unpromised concealment of a perpetrator or accomplice of a crime, as well as of instruments and means of committing a crime or traces of a crime, and failure to report a crime do not constitute complicity, and criminal liability for such acts arises only in cases provided for in this Law.

(2) A fiancé(e), spouse, parents, children, brothers and sisters, grandparents and grandchildren of the person who committed the crime, as well as a person with whom the natural person who committed the crime lives together and with whom he or she has a common (undivided) household, shall not be held liable for previously unpromised concealment and failure to report.

(3) In cases provided for by law, other persons shall also not be held liable for failure to report.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 25.09.2014 and 06.06.2019, which enter into force on 03.07.2019.)

### 23. Section. Single (Unified) Criminal Offence

(1) A single (unified) criminal offence is one act (action or omission) that has the characteristics of one criminal offence, or two or more interrelated criminal offences covered by a single intent of the guilty person and which correspond to the characteristics of only one criminal offence.

(2) A single (unified) criminal offence also comprises continuing and continuous criminal offences.

(3) A single continuing criminal offence comprises several interrelated identical criminal actions directed towards a common objective, if they are covered by a single intent of the guilty person, and therefore in their totality they constitute one criminal offence.

(4) A single continuous criminal offence is the continuous commission of one criminal offence (action or omission), which is connected with the subsequent continuous failure to fulfil the obligations that the law has imposed on the guilty person under threat of criminal prosecution.

(5) (Deleted by the Law of 13.12.2012)
(With amendments made by the Law of 13.12.2012, which enters into force on 01.04.2013.)

### 24. Section. Plurality of Criminal Offences

(1) Plurality of criminal offences exists when one person commits (or permits) two or more independent acts (action or omission) that correspond to the characteristics of several criminal offences, or when a person commits (or permits) one act (action or omission) that corresponds to the characteristics of at least two different criminal offences.

(2) Plurality of criminal offences comprises aggregate of criminal offences and recidivism.

(3) Plurality of criminal offences also comprises such criminal offences for which a sentence imposed abroad is being executed in Latvia.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 20.06.2002 and 13.12.2012, which enters into force on 01.04.2013.)

### 25. Section. Repetition of Criminal Offences

(Deleted by the Law of 13.12.2012, which enters into force on 01.04.2013.)

### 26. Section. Aggregate of Criminal Offences

(1) An aggregate of criminal offences comprises one act or several acts committed by one person that correspond to the characteristics of two or more criminal offences, if this person has not been convicted of any of these criminal offences and the limitation period for criminal liability has not expired either.

(2) An act committed by a person that corresponds to the characteristics of several different interrelated criminal offences constitutes an ideal aggregate of criminal offences.

(3) Two or more unrelated acts committed by a person that correspond to the characteristics of several criminal offences constitute a real aggregate of criminal offences.

(4) An act for the commission of which a person has been released from criminal liability does not constitute an aggregate of criminal offences.

(5) If one criminal offence corresponds to both a general and a special provision provided for in the Special Part of this Law, then an aggregate of criminal offences does not arise and criminal liability arises only in accordance with the special provision.
(With amendments made by the Law of 13.12.2012, which enters into force on 01.04.2013.)

### 27. Section. Recidivism of Criminal Offences

Recidivism of a criminal offence comprises a new intentional criminal offence committed by a person after this person's conviction for a previously committed intentional criminal offence, if the criminal record for it has not been removed or has not been expunged in the manner prescribed by law at the time of committing the new criminal offence.
(In the wording of the Law of 12.11.2015, which enters into force on 02.12.2015.)

Chapter III
Circumstances Excluding Criminal Liability

### 28. Section. Types of Circumstances Excluding Criminal Liability

Circumstances that exclude criminal liability, even though actions committed in these circumstances correspond to the characteristics of a criminal offence provided for in this Law, are necessary defence, apprehension causing harm to a person, extreme necessity, justifiable professional risk and execution of a criminal order or criminal instruction.

### 29. Section. Necessary Defence

(1) Necessary defence is an action committed in defence of state or public interests, one's own or another person's rights, as well as a person against an attack or threat of attack in such a way that harm is caused to the attacker. Criminal liability for this action arises if the limits of necessary defence have been exceeded.

(2) Exceeding the limits of necessary defence is recognised as an obvious disproportion of the defence to the nature and danger of the attack, as a result of which harm is caused to the attacker that was not necessary to prevent or repel the attack.

(3) Causing harm to an attacker through negligence while repelling an attack is not criminally punishable.

(4) A person has the right to necessary defence regardless of the possibility to avoid the attack or to seek assistance from other persons.

### 30. Section. Putative Defence

(1) Putative defence exists when the real attack referred to in Section 29 of this Law does not occur, but the person mistakenly believes that such an attack is occurring.

(2) In cases where the circumstances of the incident have given grounds to assume that a real attack is occurring, but the person who applied defensive measures was not aware that such assumption was mistaken, and moreover could not and should not have been aware of it, the actions of this person are assessed as necessary defence.

(3) A person who has exceeded the limits of defence that would be permissible in circumstances of a corresponding real attack is liable as for exceeding the limits of necessary defence.

(4) A person who causes harm corresponding to the characteristics of a criminal offence to a putative attacker without being aware of the putative nature of the attack, although in the specific circumstances he or she should have and could have been aware of it, is liable for the respective act as one committed through negligence.

### 31. Section. Apprehension Causing Harm to a Person

(1) Apprehension causing harm to a person is an action directed against a person who is committing or has committed a criminal offence. Criminal liability for this action does not arise if there has been no obvious disproportion of the harm caused to the person to the nature of the act, failure to submit or resistance.

(2) A person who, in carrying out apprehension, has violated the conditions of apprehension is liable for the violation of these conditions.

(3) If the actions by which harm is caused to the person to be apprehended were not necessary for his or her apprehension, liability for the harm caused arises on general grounds.

(4) Causing harm to a person to be apprehended through negligence is not criminally punishable.

### 32. Section. Extreme Necessity

Extreme necessity is an action that a person commits to prevent harm that threatens state or public interests, the rights of this person or another person, as well as these or other persons, if the respective harm could not be prevented by other means in the specific circumstances and if the harm caused is less than the harm prevented. Extreme necessity excludes criminal liability.

### 33. Section. Justified professional risk

(1) Criminal liability does not arise for harm caused by professional activity that has the characteristics of a criminal offence if this activity was carried out to achieve a socially beneficial purpose that could not be achieved in any other way. The professional risk associated with this activity shall be considered justified if the person who took the risk has done everything to prevent harm to legally protected interests.

(2) Risk shall not be recognised as justified if it is knowingly associated with a threat to the lives of several persons or with threats to cause an ecological catastrophe or public disaster.

### 34. Section. Execution of a criminal order and a criminal instruction

(1) The execution of a criminal order or a criminal instruction is justifiable for the person who executed it only in cases where this person was not aware of the criminal nature of the order or instruction and it was not obvious. Criminal liability in such cases nevertheless arises when crimes against humanity and peace, war crimes and genocide have been committed.

(2) A person who has not executed a criminal order or instruction shall not be held criminally liable.

IV Chapter Punishment

### 35. Section. Punishment and its purpose

(1) The punishment provided for in the Criminal Law is a coercive measure which, in the name of the State, is imposed by a court on a person who is guilty of committing a criminal offence within the framework of this Law or, in cases provided for by law, is determined by a prosecutor by drawing up a penal order.

(2) The purpose of punishment is:

1) to protect public safety;

2) to restore justice;

3) to punish the guilty person for the criminal offence committed;

4) to resocialise the punished person;

5) to ensure that the convicted person and other persons comply with the law and refrain from committing criminal offences.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 28.09.2005 and 13.12.2012, which enter into force on 01.04.2013.)

### 36. Section. Types of punishment

(1) A person who has committed a criminal offence may be sentenced to one of the following principal punishments:

1) (deleted by the Law of 01.12.2011);

2) deprivation of liberty;

3) (deleted by the Law of 13.12.2012);

4) (deleted by the Law of 13.12.2012);

41) probation supervision;

5) community service;

6) fine.

(2) In addition to the principal punishment, the following additional punishments may be imposed on the convicted person:

1) confiscation of property;

2) expulsion from the Republic of Latvia;

3) probation supervision;

4) community service;

5) fine;

6) restriction of rights.

(3) For a person who has committed a criminal violation, a less serious crime or a serious crime for which deprivation of liberty of up to five years is provided, a prosecutor, by drawing up a penal order, may impose probation supervision, community service or a fine, as well as additional punishments — community service, a fine or

restriction of rights.

(4) The procedure for serving punishment shall be determined in accordance with law.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 12.02.2004, 28.09.2005, 08.12.2005, 21.05.2009, 08.07.2011, 01.12.2011,
13.12.2012, 0.03.2016 and 17.12.2020, which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 37. Section. Death penalty

(Deleted by the Law of 01.12.2011, which enters into force on 01.01.2012.)

### 38. Section. Deprivation of liberty

(1) Deprivation of liberty is the compulsory detention of a person in imprisonment.

(2) Deprivation of liberty shall be imposed for a period from fifteen days to twenty years.

(21) In cases specifically provided for in this Law for criminal violations and crimes for which this Law provides for deprivation of liberty for a period not exceeding five years, short-term deprivation of liberty may be imposed for a period of up to three months.

(3) In cases specifically provided for in this Law, deprivation of liberty may be imposed for life (life imprisonment).

(4) The period of deprivation of liberty shall be determined in years, months and days.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 16.06.2009, 13.12.2012, 25.09.2014 and 12.11.2015, which enters into force on 02.12.2015.)

38. 1 Section. Probation supervision

(1) Probation supervision as a principal punishment or additional punishment is the compulsory involvement of a person in social behaviour correction and social rehabilitation measures appropriate to their age, psychological characteristics and level of development.

(2) Probation supervision as a principal punishment may be applied only in the cases mentioned in the Special Part of this Law for a period from one year to five years.

(3) Probation supervision as an additional punishment may be applied only together with deprivation of liberty in the cases mentioned in the Special Part of this Law for a period from one year to three years. In cases specifically provided for in the Special Part of this Law, probation supervision as an additional punishment may also be applied to a person for a longer period, but not exceeding five years. According to the nature of the criminal offence, the court may also impose probation supervision as an additional punishment in cases where this punishment is not provided for in the sanction of the relevant article of the Special Part of this Law, for a period from one year to three years.

(4) The convicted person or the person for whom probation supervision has been imposed by a prosecutor's penal order shall, during the probation supervision period, fulfil the obligations provided for in the law regulating the execution of criminal punishments and imposed by the sentence execution institution.

(5) The execution of probation supervision as an additional punishment shall commence after serving the punishment of deprivation of liberty. If a person has been conditionally released before the term from serving the punishment of deprivation of liberty, the execution of probation supervision as an additional punishment shall commence from the moment when the supervision of the person after conditional early release has ended.

(6) The court, upon receipt of a submission from the sentence execution institution, may reduce the term of probation supervision or cancel probation supervision if the person for whom probation supervision has been imposed by a court judgment or a prosecutor's penal order has served half of the imposed punishment term, has exemplarily fulfilled the obligations provided for in the law regulating the execution of criminal punishments and imposed by the sentence execution institution, and has cooperated with the sentence execution institution in resolving identified criminogenic problems and achieving socially supportive goals.

(7) If a person for whom probation supervision has been imposed by a court judgment or a prosecutor's penal order fails to fulfil, without justifiable reason, the obligations provided for in the law regulating the execution of criminal punishments or imposed by the sentence execution institution, the court, upon receipt of a submission from the sentence execution institution, shall replace the unserved period of punishment, counting one day of probation supervision as one day of deprivation of liberty, but not exceeding:

1) three months if probation supervision was imposed for a criminal violation;

2) three years if probation supervision was imposed for a less serious crime;

3) five years if probation supervision was imposed for a serious or particularly serious crime.
(In the wording of the Law of 17.12.2020 with amendments made by the Law of 07.04.2022, which enters into force on 04.05.2022.)

### 40. Section. Community Service

(1)	Community service as a principal or supplementary punishment is the compulsory involvement of a person in work necessary for society that is appropriate to their age, psychological characteristics, physical abilities and level of development, performed during time free from main work or studies and without remuneration.

(2)	Community service as a principal punishment shall be imposed for a period from forty to two hundred and eighty hours. Community service as a supplementary punishment for a period from forty to one hundred hours may be imposed on a person who has been conditionally convicted or for whom probation supervision has been imposed as a principal punishment.

(3)	Community service shall not be applicable to persons who are unable to perform it due to physical or mental disorders.

(4)	Upon the proposal of the sentence execution institution, the court may release from serving the sentence a person who has been convicted to community service or for whom community service has been imposed by a prosecutor's penal order, if the community service has been imposed for a period not less than eighty hours, if at least half of the imposed sentence has actually been served and the person has fulfilled the obligations provided for in the law regulating the execution of criminal sentences, has observed the conditions and procedure for the performance of community service, and has also performed the community service in an exemplary manner.

(5)	If a person who has been convicted to community service, or a person for whom community service has been imposed by a prosecutor's penal order, fails to perform it without justifiable reason, the court, upon receipt of an application from the sentence execution institution, shall replace the unserved sentence with short-term deprivation of liberty, calculating four working hours as one day of short-term deprivation of liberty, but not longer than three months.
(In the wording of the law of 17.12.2020. with amendments made by the law of 07.04.2022., which enters into force on 04.05.2022.)

### 41. Section. Fine

(1)	A fine as a principal or supplementary punishment is a sum of money that the court or prosecutor imposes to be paid to the state within 30 days in the amounts specified in this Section.

(2)	A fine as a principal punishment, according to the harmfulness of the criminal offence and the financial situation of the guilty person, shall be imposed:

1)	for a criminal violation — in the amount of one to one hundred minimum monthly wages established in the Republic of Latvia;

2)	for a less serious crime — in the amount of three to one thousand minimum monthly wages established in the Republic of Latvia;

3)	for a serious crime for which this law provides for deprivation of liberty for a period not exceeding five years — in the amount of ten to two thousand minimum monthly wages established in the Republic of Latvia.

(21)	A fine shall be imposed in the amount of minimum monthly wages established in the Republic of Latvia as it is on the day of issuing the judgment, indicating in the judgment the amount of this fine in the monetary units of the Republic of Latvia.

(22)	According to the harmfulness of the criminal offence and the financial situation of the guilty person, the court may impose a fine as a principal punishment also for the commission of a serious crime for which this law provides for deprivation of liberty for a period exceeding five years, and for the commission of a particularly serious crime, if the crime has not caused a person's death, has not caused serious bodily injury to at least one person or less serious bodily injury to several persons, is not related to violence or threat of violence, is not related to illegal circulation of narcotic and psychotropic substances and has not been committed in an organised group, in the amount of three hundred to ten thousand minimum monthly wages established in the Republic of Latvia.

(3)	A fine as a supplementary punishment, according to the harmfulness of the criminal offence and the financial situation of the guilty person, shall be imposed:

1)	for a criminal violation — in the amount of one to one hundred minimum monthly wages established in the Republic of Latvia;

2)	for a less serious crime — in the amount of three to one thousand minimum monthly wages established in the Republic of Latvia;

3)	for a serious crime for which this law provides for deprivation of liberty for a period not exceeding five years — in the amount of five to two thousand minimum monthly wages established in the Republic of Latvia;

4)	for a serious crime for which this law provides for deprivation of liberty for a period exceeding five years, and for a particularly serious crime — in the amount of ten to five thousand minimum monthly wages established in the Republic of Latvia.

(4)	The financial situation of the guilty person shall be determined by assessing their ability to immediately pay the fine or to obtain foreseeable income that would allow them to pay the imposed fine within the time period established by law.

(5)	The payment of the fine may be divided into instalments or deferred by the court or prosecutor respectively for a period not exceeding one year from the day when the judgment or penal order has entered into legal force. If the fine exceeds three hundred minimum monthly wages, its payment may be divided into instalments or deferred by the court or prosecutor respectively for a period not exceeding three years from the day when the judgment or penal order has entered into legal force.

(6)	A fine not paid within the established time, if it does not exceed thirty minimum monthly wages, shall be replaced with short-term deprivation of liberty, calculating one minimum monthly wage as four days of short-term deprivation of liberty, but not more than three months; a fine not paid, if it does not exceed two hundred minimum monthly wages, shall be replaced with deprivation of liberty, calculating one minimum monthly wage as four days of deprivation of liberty, but not more than one year; a fine not paid, if it exceeds two hundred minimum monthly wages, shall be replaced with deprivation of liberty, calculating one minimum monthly wage as five days of deprivation of liberty, but not more than five years.

(7)	If the fine or part thereof is paid at a time when the convicted person is serving a sentence of deprivation of liberty instead of the fine, they shall be released or the term of deprivation of liberty shall be reduced according to the part of the fine paid. When reducing the term of the sentence in the manner indicated, the time of deprivation of liberty shall be credited according to the proportion established by the court.
(In the wording of the law of 16.06.2009. with amendments made by the laws of 13.12.2012., 12.11.2015., 29.10.2015., 10.03.2016.,
08.06.2017., 06.06.2019., 11.06.2020., 06.07.2021. and 07.04.2022., which enters into force on 04.05.2022.)

### 42. Section. Confiscation of Property

(1)	Confiscation of property is the compulsory uncompensated alienation to state ownership of property in the ownership of the convicted person. Confiscation as a supplementary punishment may be imposed. Property in the ownership of the convicted person that they have transferred to another natural or legal person may also be confiscated.

(2)	Confiscation of property may be imposed only in the cases provided for in the Special Part of this law.

(3)	The court, when imposing confiscation of property, shall specifically indicate what property is to be confiscated.

(4)	The law establishes the property necessary for the convicted person or persons in their care that is not subject to confiscation.
(In the wording of the law of 12.02.2004. with amendments made by the laws of 06.10.2005., 21.05.2009., 13.12.2012. and 22.06.2017., which enters into force on 01.08.2017.)

### 43. Section. Expulsion from the Republic of Latvia

(1)	A citizen of another state or a person who has a permanent residence permit in another state may be expelled from the Republic of Latvia if the court finds that, taking into account the circumstances of the case and the personality of the guilty person, his or her presence in the Republic of Latvia is not permissible.

(11) Expulsion from the Republic of Latvia is not applicable to a citizen of a European Union Member State, a European Economic Area state or the Swiss Confederation, as well as his or her spouse, children up to the age of twenty-one, parents or a person with whom he or she lives together and with whom he or she has a common (undivided) household or who

is in his or her care, except in cases where the court finds that, taking into account the circumstances of the case, the nature of the criminal offence and the personality of the guilty person, his or her presence in the Republic of Latvia poses a serious threat to public order or state security. If such a person has resided in the Republic of Latvia for the previous ten years or is a minor, then expulsion in respect of him or her shall be applied only if the court finds that, taking into account the circumstances of the case, the nature of the criminal offence and the personality of the guilty person, his or her presence in the Republic of Latvia poses a serious threat to state security. Expulsion from the Republic of Latvia in respect of a minor shall also be applied if it is in the interests of the minor in accordance with international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia.

(2)	This penalty may be imposed as an additional penalty together with deprivation of liberty or a fine, establishing a prohibition on entry for a period from three to ten years and executing it after serving the principal penalty or after release from serving the penalty before the term in the manner prescribed by law, or after the judgment enters into force in the case of conditional conviction. The period of serving the additional penalty shall be counted from the day the person is expelled from the Republic of Latvia.
(With amendments made by the laws of 13.12.2007., 13.12.2012. and 16.10.2014., which enter into force on 01.02.2015.)

### 44. Section. Restriction of Rights

(1)	Restriction of rights is the deprivation of certain rights or the establishment of a prohibition that does not allow a person to exercise certain rights, hold a certain position, perform a certain professional or other type of activity, visit certain places or events.

(2)	Restriction of rights is an additional penalty imposed by a court or, when drawing up a penalty order, determined by a prosecutor for a period from one year to five years, depriving the rights specified in the relevant section of the Special Part of this law or establishing a prohibition. Taking into account the type and nature of the criminal offence, in cases specifically provided for in the Special Part of this law, a person's rights may also be restricted for a longer period, but not longer than ten years.

(3)	In accordance with the nature of the criminal offence, restriction of rights may also be established in cases where this penalty is not provided for in the sanction of the relevant section of the Special Part of this law, or in addition to the restriction of rights provided for in the sanction of the relevant section of the Special Part of this law, another restriction of rights may also be established.

(4)	If a person is convicted with deprivation of liberty and with restriction of rights, then the prohibition referred to in this section applies both to the time when the person is serving the deprivation of liberty, as well as to the period of serving the additional penalty specified in the judgment, counting from the day he or she finishes serving the principal penalty. When establishing this additional penalty together with conditional deprivation of liberty, the period of serving the additional penalty shall be counted from the day the established probationary period begins for the person. When establishing this additional penalty together with other types of principal penalty, the period of serving the additional penalty shall be counted from the day the conviction judgment or the prosecutor's penalty order enters into force.
(In the wording of the law of 13.12.2012. with amendments made by the laws of 12.11.2015., 10.03.2016. and 05.10.2023., which enter into force on 20.10.2023.)

Chapter V Determination of Penalty

### 46. Section. General Principles of Determination of Penalty

(1)	The penalty shall be determined in the amount provided for the committed criminal offence by the sanction of the relevant section of the Special Part of this law, observing the provisions of the General Part of this law.

(2)	When determining the type of penalty, the nature of the committed criminal offence and the harm caused, as well as the personality of the guilty person, shall be taken into account.

(3)	When determining the measure of penalty, circumstances mitigating and aggravating liability shall be taken into account.

(31) If the sanction of a section of the Special Part of this law for the committed crime provides only one principal penalty — deprivation of liberty, when determining its duration, the nature of the criminal offence, the harm caused, the personality of the guilty person, as well as circumstances mitigating and aggravating liability shall be taken into account.

(4)	The penalty of deprivation of liberty for a criminal violation and a less serious crime shall be applied if the objective of the penalty cannot be achieved by establishing one of the lighter types of penalty provided for in the sanction of the relevant section.
(In the wording of the law of 13.12.2012. with amendments made by the law of 07.04.2022., which enters into force on 04.05.2022.)

### 47. Section. Circumstances Mitigating Liability

(1)	The following circumstances shall be recognised as mitigating liability:

1)	the perpetrator of the criminal offence has reported himself or herself as guilty, sincerely confessed and regretted what was committed;

2)	the guilty person actively facilitated the disclosure and investigation of the criminal offence;

3)	the guilty person voluntarily compensated the victim for the harm caused by the criminal offence or eliminated the harm caused;

4)	the guilty person facilitated the disclosure of another person's crime;

5)	the criminal offence was committed under the influence of unlawful or immoral conduct of the victim;

6)	the criminal offence was committed in violation of the conditions of lawfulness of necessary defence, extreme necessity, apprehension of a person who has committed a criminal offence, justified professional risk, execution of an order and instruction;

7)	the criminal offence was committed by a person in a state of limited sanity.

(2)	When determining the penalty, another circumstance related to the committed criminal offence that is not provided for in this law may also be recognised as a circumstance mitigating liability.

(3)	A circumstance that is provided for in this law as a feature of the elements of a criminal offence shall not be recognised as a circumstance mitigating liability.
(With amendments made by the law of 13.12.2012., which enters into force on 01.04.2013.)

(2)	Ja visi noziedzīgie nodarījumi, kas veido noziedzīgu nodarījumu kopību, ir kriminālpārkāpumi vai mazāk smagi noziegumi, galīgais sods nosakāms, ietverot vieglāko sodu smagākajā vai arī pilnīgi vai daļēji saskaitot piespriestos sodus. Šādā gadījumā kopējais soda apmērs vai laiks drīkst pārsniegt maksimālo soda apmēru vai laiku, kāds paredzēts par smagāko no izdarītajiem noziedzīgajiem nodarījumiem, bet ne vairāk kā par pusi no maksimālā soda apmēra vai laika, kāds paredzēts par smagāko no izdarītajiem noziedzīgajiem nodarījumiem.

(3)	Ja vismaz viens noziedzīgais nodarījums, kas veido noziedzīgu nodarījumu kopību, ir smags vai sevišķi smags noziegums, galīgais sods tiek noteikts, pilnīgi vai daļēji saskaitot piespriestos sodus. Šādā gadījumā kopējais soda apmērs vai laiks drīkst pārsniegt maksimālo soda apmēru vai laiku, kāds paredzēts par smagāko no izdarītajiem noziedzīgajiem nodarījumiem, bet ne vairāk kā par pusi no maksimālā soda apmēra vai laika, kāds paredzēts par smagāko no izdarītajiem noziedzīgajiem nodarījumiem. Saskaitīto brīvības atņemšanas sodu (izņemot mūža ieslodzījumu) kopējais laiks nedrīkst pārsniegt divdesmit piecus gadus, bet, ja izdarīts sevišķi smags noziegums, kura rezultātā iestājusies cietušā nāve, brīvības atņemšanas soda kopējo laiku var noteikt arī uz visu mūžu (mūža ieslodzījums).

(4)	Papildsods, tāpat kā pamatsods, vispirms nosakāms atsevišķi par katru noziedzīgo nodarījumu, bet pēc tam pēc noziedzīgu nodarījumu kopības kopā ar pamatsodu. Pēc noziedzīgu nodarījumu kopības noteiktajam pamatsodam pievieno papildsodus, kas piespriesti atsevišķi par katru noziedzīgo nodarījumu.

(41) Ja pamatsods un papildsods atbilst vienam soda veidam, tad tie pilnīgi vai daļēji saskaitāmi, galīgo sodu nosakot kā pamatsodu. Šādā gadījumā kopējais soda apmērs vai laiks drīkst pārsniegt attiecīgajam pamatsoda veidam paredzēto maksimālo apmēru vai laiku, bet ne vairāk par pusi no tā.

(5)	Tādā pašā kārtībā tiesa nosaka sodu, ja pēc sprieduma vai prokurora priekšraksta par sodu spēkā stāšanās konstatēts, ka persona vainīga vēl citā noziedzīgā nodarījumā, ko tā izdarījusi pirms sprieduma vai prokurora priekšraksta par sodu spēkā stāšanās pirmajā lietā. Šajā gadījumā soda laikā ieskaitāms sods, kas pilnīgi vai daļēji jau izciests pēc pirmā sprieduma vai prokurora priekšraksta par sodu. Ja brīvības atņemšanas laiks, kas spriedumā noteikts nosacīti, ir lielāks par citā spriedumā noteikto brīvības atņemšanas laiku, tad brīvības atņemšanas laiks, kas noteikts nosacīti, pilnīgi vai daļēji saskaitāms ar brīvības atņemšanas laiku.

(6)	Šā panta kārtībā noteiktā galīgā soda kopējais apmērs vai laiks drīkst pārsniegt attiecīgajam soda veidam noteikto maksimālo apmēru vai laiku.

### 50. pants. Determination of punishment for several criminal offences

(1)	If a person has committed several independent criminal offences, the court, when rendering a judgment, or the prosecutor, when drawing up a penal order, shall determine the punishment separately for each criminal offence. In such case, the final punishment shall be determined according to the aggregate of criminal offences, by absorbing the lighter punishment into the more severe one or by fully or partially adding together the imposed punishments.

(2)	If all the criminal offences that constitute an aggregate of criminal offences are criminal violations or less serious crimes, the final punishment shall be determined by absorbing the lighter punishment into the more severe one or by fully or partially adding together the imposed punishments. In such case, the total amount or term of the punishment may exceed the maximum amount or term of the punishment provided for the most serious of the committed criminal offences, but not more than by half of the maximum amount or term of the punishment provided for the most serious of the committed criminal offences.

(3)	If at least one criminal offence that constitutes an aggregate of criminal offences is a serious or particularly serious crime, the final punishment shall be determined by fully or partially adding together the imposed punishments. In such case, the total amount or term of the punishment may exceed the maximum amount or term of the punishment provided for the most serious of the committed criminal offences, but not more than by half of the maximum amount or term of the punishment provided for the most serious of the committed criminal offences. The total term of added custodial sentences (except life imprisonment) may not exceed twenty-five years, but if a particularly serious crime has been committed as a result of which the death of the victim has occurred, the total term of the custodial sentence may also be determined for life (life imprisonment).

(4)	An additional punishment, like the principal punishment, shall first be determined separately for each criminal offence, but thereafter according to the aggregate of criminal offences together with the principal punishment. To the principal punishment determined according to the aggregate of criminal offences shall be added the additional punishments that have been imposed separately for each criminal offence.

(41) If the principal punishment and the additional punishment correspond to one type of punishment, then they shall be fully or partially added together, determining the final punishment as a principal punishment. In such case, the total amount or term of the punishment may exceed the maximum amount or term provided for the respective type of principal punishment, but not more than by half of it.

(5)	In the same manner the court shall determine the punishment if, after the entry into force of the judgment or the prosecutor's penal order, it is established that the person is guilty of another criminal offence that he or she committed before the entry into force of the judgment or the prosecutor's penal order in the first case. In this case, the punishment that has already been fully or partially served pursuant to the first judgment or the prosecutor's penal order shall be included in the term of the punishment. If the term of deprivation of liberty that has been determined conditionally in the judgment is greater than the term of deprivation of liberty determined in another judgment, then the term of deprivation of liberty that has been determined conditionally shall be fully or partially added together with the term of deprivation of liberty.

(6)	The total amount or term of the final punishment determined in accordance with this Section may exceed the maximum amount or term determined for the respective type of punishment.
(With amendments made by the laws of 21.10.2010., 13.12.2012., 25.09.2014., 08.06.2017., 17.12.2020. and 07.04.2022.
which entered into force on 04.05.2022.)

### 51. pants. Determination of punishment according to several judgments

(1)	If a convicted person, after the entry into force of a judgment but before full serving of the punishment, has committed a new criminal offence, the court in the new judgment shall fully or partially add to the determined punishment the punishment that has not been served pursuant to the previous judgment.

(11)	When determining punishment according to several judgments, not less than one third of the unserved punishment shall be added to the punishment,
if:

1)	a person who has been punished for a serious or particularly serious crime has committed a serious or particularly serious crime during the term of the unserved punishment;

2)	recidivism of criminal offences has been established;

3)	the new criminal offence has been committed during the probation period determined by the court;

4)	the new criminal offence has been committed during the time when the person has been released conditionally before the term from serving the principal punishment.

(2)	The final punishment according to several judgments must be greater than the punishment determined for a newly committed criminal offence, as well as than the part of the unserved punishment pursuant to the previous judgment.

(3)	When adding together punishments according to several judgments, the total amount or term of the punishment may exceed the maximum amount or term determined for the respective type of punishment, but not more than by half of the maximum amount or term determined for the respective type of punishment. The total term of added custodial sentences (except life imprisonment) may not exceed thirty years, but if a particularly serious crime has been committed as a result of which the death of the victim has occurred, the total term of the custodial sentence may also be determined for life (life imprisonment).

(31) If a person sentenced to life imprisonment who has been released from serving the punishment conditionally before the term commits a criminal offence during the period of pre-term supervision, the court shall add life imprisonment to the determined punishment.

(4)	A judgment within the meaning of Sections 51 and 52 of this Law is also a prosecutor's penal order.
(With amendments made by the laws of 13.12.2007., 21.10.2010., 13.12.2012., 25.09.2014. and 11.06.2020. which
entered into force on 06.07.2020.)

### 52. Section. Rules for aggregation and substitution of punishments

(1) When aggregating punishments for several criminal offences in one judgment or following several judgments, one day of deprivation of liberty corresponds to:

1) (deleted by law of 13.12.2012.);

2) eight hours of community service;

3) (deleted by law of 08.07.2011.);

4) two days of probation supervision.

(2) A fine, restriction of rights, if these punishments are imposed together with deprivation of liberty, probation supervision or community service, shall be executed independently. In the case of conditional conviction, the additional punishment — community service — shall be executed independently, commencing with the probation period.

(21) If for several criminal offences in one judgment or following several judgments principal punishments have been imposed — community service and deprivation of liberty, the term of which together does not exceed five years —, then the punishment

— community service — shall be executed independently. In such cases the execution of community service shall commence after serving the punishment of deprivation of liberty, but in the case of conditional conviction — immediately after the judgment enters into force.

(22) If for several criminal offences in one judgment or following several judgments punishments have been imposed — community service and probation supervision —, then community service shall be executed simultaneously with probation supervision.

(23) If for several criminal offences in one judgment or following several judgments principal punishments have been imposed — probation supervision and deprivation of liberty, which has not been imposed conditionally and the term of which together does not exceed five years —, then the punishment — probation supervision — shall be executed independently. In such cases the execution of probation supervision shall commence after serving the punishment of deprivation of liberty.

(3) When imposing punishments not mentioned in the first part of this section, the court, taking into account detention, the part of the punishment served or the period of application of coercive measures of a medical nature, may mitigate the punishment or completely release the guilty person from serving the punishment.

(4) Punishment terms shall be counted in years, months and days. The court shall include detention in the punishment period, counting one day of detention as one day of deprivation of liberty. The court shall include apprehension in the punishment period, counting apprehension up to twenty-four hours as one day of deprivation of liberty. Detention that coincides in time with the serving of a punishment of deprivation of liberty for another criminal offence shall not be included in the punishment period.

(5) Detention, apprehension and the part of the punishment served shall be included in the term of the more severe punishment in accordance with the provisions of the first part of this section.

(6) House arrest shall be included in the term of deprivation of liberty. One day of house arrest corresponds to one day of deprivation of liberty.

(7) Substituted punishments shall be fully aggregated.
(With amendments made by laws of 12.06.2003., 28.09.2005., 16.06.2009., 08.07.2011., 13.12.2012., 15.05.2014.,
08.06.2017., 06.06.2019., 11.06.2020. and 17.12.2020., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 53. Section. Imposition of punishment for preparation for a crime and for an attempt to commit a crime

When imposing punishment for preparation for a crime or for an attempt to commit a crime, the court shall take into account the nature of the actions committed by the guilty person and the harm caused by them, the degree of realisation of the criminal intent and the reasons why the crime was not completed.

### 54. Section. Imposition of punishment for a criminal offence committed in complicity

(1) When imposing punishment on participants in a criminal offence, the court shall take into account the nature and role of each participant's complicity in the committed criminal offence.

(2) Aggravating and mitigating circumstances relating to an individual participant shall be taken into account by the court when imposing punishment only on that participant.

### 55. Section. Conditional conviction

(1) If, when imposing a punishment — deprivation of liberty — longer than three months, but not longer than five years, or not longer than three years if a particularly serious crime has been committed, the court, taking into account the nature of the committed criminal offence and the harm caused, the personality of the guilty person and other circumstances of the case, gains the conviction that the guilty person, without serving the punishment, will not commit offences in the future, it may convict the guilty person conditionally.

(2) In this case the court shall decide not to execute the punishment if, during the probation period determined by it, the convicted person does not commit a new criminal offence, does not violate public order and fulfils the obligations provided for in the law regulating the execution of criminal punishments and established by the punishment execution institution.

(3) When imposing a conditional conviction, the court shall determine a probation period from six months to five years. The probation period shall commence on the day the court judgment enters into force. The determined probation period may not be less than the imposed term of deprivation of liberty.

(4) When imposing a conditional conviction, the judgment shall indicate the circumstances on the basis of which the court has found it appropriate not to execute the punishment.

(5) When imposing a conditional conviction, additional punishments may be imposed. The additional punishment — probation supervision — shall be executed only if the court decides to execute the principal punishment specified in the judgment.

(6) (Deleted by law of 16.10.2014.)

(7) (Deleted by law of 16.10.2014.)

(8) (Deleted by law of 16.10.2014.)

(9) If a conditionally convicted person without justifiable reason fails to fulfil the obligations provided for in the law regulating the execution of criminal punishments or established by the punishment execution institution, the court, on the basis of a submission by the punishment execution institution, may adopt a decision on the execution of the punishment specified in the judgment for the convicted person or on the extension of the probation period by up to one year.

(10) If a conditionally convicted person commits a new criminal offence during the probation period, the punishment imposed on him or her shall be executed and the court shall impose punishment in accordance with the provisions of Sections 51 and 52 of this law.

(101) If a conditionally convicted person has committed a new criminal offence through negligence and for the new criminal offence he or she has been released from criminal liability in accordance with Section 58 of this law or released from punishment in accordance with Section 59 of this law, or for the new criminal offence a fine or community service has been imposed on him or her as the principal punishment, the court may adopt a decision on the extension of the probation period by up to one year.

(11) Conditional conviction shall not be imposed on a person for the commission of an intentional crime if the person has previously been convicted with deprivation of liberty and the conviction has not been removed or expunged in the manner prescribed by law. Conditional conviction shall not be imposed on a person who has committed a crime provided for in Section 159 or 160 of this law.

### 56. Section. Statute of Limitations for Criminal Liability

(1)	A person may not be brought to criminal liability if the following time has elapsed since the day on which he or she committed the criminal offence:

1)	(deleted by the law of 21.10.2010.);

2)	two years from the day of commission of a criminal violation;

3)	five years from the day of commission of a less serious crime;

4)	ten years from the day of commission of a serious crime;

5)	fifteen years from the day of commission of a particularly serious crime, except for a crime for which life imprisonment may be imposed in accordance with law;

6)	(deleted by the law of 12.11.2015.).

(11) A person may not be brought to criminal liability if twenty years have elapsed since the day on which the victim in a criminal offence directed against the morality and sexual inviolability of a minor or by which serious bodily injury associated with genital mutilation or loss of reproductive capacity has been inflicted, or in human trafficking, or in coercion to undergo an abortion, reached the age of eighteen, except for a crime for which life imprisonment may be imposed in accordance with law.

(2)	The limitation period is calculated from the day on which the criminal offence was committed, or in the case provided for in Paragraph 1.1 of this Section from the day on which the victim reached the age of eighteen, until the delivery of the indictment or the notification of an official extradition request to the accused, if the accused is staying in another country and a search for him or her has been announced.

(3)	The limitation period is interrupted if, before the expiry of the time limits specified in Paragraph 1 or 1.1 of this Section, the person who committed the criminal offence commits a new criminal offence. In this case, the limitation period provided for the most serious of the criminal offences committed begins to run from the moment of commission of the new criminal offence.

(4)	The question of the application of the statute of limitations to a person who has committed a crime for which life imprisonment may be imposed shall be decided by a court if thirty years have elapsed since the day of commission of the crime or since the day on which the victim in a crime directed against the morality and sexual inviolability of a minor reached the age of eighteen.
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.05.2004., 28.09.2005., 12.10.2006., 21.10.2010., 01.12.2011., 13.12.2012.,
12.11.2015. and 08.06.2017., which enters into force on 01.01.2018.)

### 57. Section. Non-Application of Statute of Limitations

The statute of limitations for criminal liability does not apply to a person who has committed a crime against humanity, a crime against peace, a war crime or has participated in genocide.

### 58. Section. Release from Criminal Liability

(1)	A person who has committed a minor criminal offence may be released from criminal liability.

(2)	A person who has committed a criminal violation or a less serious crime, except for criminal offences resulting in the death of a person, may be released from criminal liability if there is a reconciliation with the victim or his or her representative and the person has not been released from criminal liability in the last year for the commission of an intentional criminal offence by concluding a reconciliation, and has fully remedied the harm caused by the committed criminal offence or compensated for the damage caused.

(3)	An accused person who has substantially assisted in the detection of a serious or particularly serious crime committed by another person, which is more serious or more dangerous than the criminal offence committed by him or her, may be released from criminal liability if this other person has been brought to criminal liability for this crime. This condition does not apply to a person who is being brought to criminal liability for the commission of a particularly serious crime provided for in Sections 116, 117, 118, 125, 159,
160, 176, 190.1, 251, 252 and 253.1 of this Law, or to a person who has himself or herself created or led an organised group or gang.

(4)	A person may also be released from criminal liability in cases specifically provided for in the Special Part of this Law.

(5)	A person may be released from criminal liability if it is established that his or her right to completion of criminal proceedings within a reasonable time has not been observed.

(6)	A person may be released from criminal liability if he or she committed a criminal offence at a time when he or she was subjected to human trafficking and was forced to commit it.
(With amendments made by the laws of 25.04.2002., 28.09.2005., 21.05.2009., 21.10.2010., 13.12.2012., 11.06.2020. and
07.04.2022., which enters into force on 04.05.2022.)

(11) A prosecutor may also conditionally release from criminal liability, in the manner prescribed by law, a person who is accused of committing a serious crime, who has not been convicted of an intentional criminal offence, and against whom criminal proceedings have not been terminated in the last five years

by conditionally releasing him or her from criminal liability, and who has substantially assisted in the detection of a serious or particularly serious crime committed by another person, which is more serious or more dangerous than the criminal offence committed by him or her, if this other person has been brought to criminal liability for this crime. This condition does not apply to a person who is being brought to criminal liability for the commission of a serious crime provided for in Sections 125, 159, 160, 176, 190.1, 251, 252 and 253.1 of this Law, or to a person who has himself or herself been the organiser of the crime.

(2)	When conditionally releasing from criminal liability, a prosecutor decides not to continue the criminal prosecution of the person for this offence if during the probationary period he or she does not commit a new criminal offence and fulfils the imposed obligations, and also, if a reconciliation has been concluded, fulfils its conditions.

(3)	When conditionally releasing from criminal liability, a prosecutor sets a probationary period for the person from three to eighteen months. The probationary period begins on the day on which the prosecutor's decision enters into force.

2)	remedy the harm caused within a specified time limit;

### 59. Section. Release from Punishment or Serving of Punishment

(1)	The release of a convicted person from punishment or serving of punishment, as well as mitigation of the imposed punishment, except for release from punishment or mitigation of punishment by way of amnesty and pardon, may be carried out only by a court in the cases and procedure specified by law.

(2)	The court may release a person who has not reached the age of majority from punishment in the cases provided for in this law, by imposing compulsory measures of an educational nature.

(3)	The court may also release a person from punishment in the cases provided for in Section 58 of this law.

(4)	The court may release from serving of punishment a person who has committed a criminal violation or a less serious crime due to dependence on alcohol, narcotic, psychotropic or toxic substances, if this person has consented to undergo treatment for dependence on alcohol, narcotic, psychotropic or toxic substances. The punishment shall be enforced if the person has not commenced treatment within the time period set by the court or has subsequently evaded treatment.

(5)	If a person who has been convicted of a criminal offence or for whom punishment has been imposed by a prosecutor's penal order, after the pronouncement of the judgment or after the prosecutor has issued the penal order, has fallen ill with a mental illness that has deprived them of the ability to understand their actions or to control them, the court shall release this person from serving of punishment. Compulsory measures of a medical nature may be imposed on them in accordance with the conditions provided for in this law.

(6)	If a person who has been convicted of a criminal offence or for whom punishment has been imposed by a prosecutor's penal order suffers from another serious, incurable illness, the court may release this person from serving of punishment.
(With amendments made by the laws of 27.05.2004., 13.12.2007. and 13.12.2012., which enter into force on 01.04.2013.)

### 60. Section. Reduction of Punishment in Exceptional Cases

If the convicted person has assisted in disclosing a crime committed by another person that is equally serious, more serious or more dangerous than the criminal offence committed by them, and this other person has been brought to criminal liability for this crime, the court may reduce the punishment imposed in the judgment, but replace the imposed life imprisonment with deprivation of liberty for twenty years.
(In the wording of the law of 07.04.2022., which enters into force on 04.05.2022.)
