### 66. Section. Application of Educational Coercive Measures to Minors

(1)	Taking into account the special circumstances of the commission of the criminal offence and the information obtained about the personality of the guilty person, which mitigates his or her liability, the court may release the minor from the imposed sentence by applying the educational coercive measures provided for by law.

(2)	The sentence shall be executed if the minor who has been released from it fails to fulfil the obligations imposed by the court during the period of the imposed sentence.
(As amended by the Law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

66.1 Section. Application of Deprivation of Liberty

(1)	Deprivation of liberty is the placement of a minor in an educational institution and includes a set of social behaviour correction and social rehabilitation measures and rules of conduct provided for in the law regulating the execution of criminal sentences appropriate to the age, psychological characteristics and level of development of the minor.

(2)	The term of deprivation of liberty may not exceed ten years — for particularly serious crimes; five years — for serious crimes involving violence or threat of violence or causing serious consequences; two years — for other serious crimes.

(3)	Deprivation of liberty shall not be applied for criminal violations and less serious crimes.

(4)	If a person has committed a criminal offence before reaching the age of eighteen for which the minimum limit of the applicable deprivation of liberty sentence is provided for in the sanction of the relevant article of the Special Part of this Law, the court may impose a sentence that is lower than this minimum limit, even in cases where it has found that the criminal offence was committed in circumstances aggravating liability.

(5)	Deprivation of liberty for a minor shall always be applied together with an additional sentence — probation supervision, including in cases where this additional sentence is not provided for in the sanction of the relevant article of the Special Part of this Law.
(As worded by the Law of 17.12.2020, which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

66.2 Section. Application of Probation Supervision

(1)	In accordance with the harmfulness of the criminal offence, the court may impose probation supervision as a principal sentence on a minor for a period from three years to six years also for the commission of such a serious crime for which this Law provides for deprivation of liberty for a period longer than five years, and for the commission of a particularly serious crime.

(2)	The court, on the basis of a submission by the sentence execution institution, may adopt a decision that a minor for whom probation supervision has been imposed as a sentence by a court judgment or prosecutor's order on punishment shall be placed in a social correction educational institution for a period of up to three years, but not less than one year, taking into account the unfavourable social environment in which the minor is located, possible threat to the minor's health or life, or other reasons that prevent the execution of probation supervision.

(3)	If a minor for whom probation supervision has been imposed as a sentence by a court judgment or prosecutor's order on punishment or for whom community service has been replaced with probation supervision in the manner provided for in this Law, without justifiable reason fails to fulfil the obligations provided for in the law regulating the execution of criminal sentences or imposed by the sentence execution institution, the court, on the basis of a submission by the sentence execution institution, may replace the unserved term of the sentence with deprivation of liberty, counting two days of probation supervision as one day of deprivation of liberty.
(As worded by the Law of 17.12.2020, which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

66.3 Section. Replacement of Community Service

If a minor who has been sentenced to community service or a minor for whom community service has been imposed by a prosecutor's order on punishment, without justifiable reason fails to perform the community service, the court, on the basis of a submission by the sentence execution institution, shall replace the unserved sentence with probation supervision for one year.
(As worded by the Law of 17.12.2020, which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

66.4 Section. Application of Fine

(1)	A fine shall be applicable only to those minors who have their own income. A fine for minors shall be applicable from one to fifty minimum monthly wages established in the Republic of Latvia.

(2)	A fine not paid within the specified time shall be replaced for a minor with community service, counting one minimum monthly wage as forty hours of community service, but not more than two hundred and eighty hours.
(As worded by the Law of 17.12.2020, as amended by the Law of 07.04.2022, which enters into force on 04.05.2022.)

66.5 Section. Other Issues Related to Imposition of Sentence

(1)	For a person who has committed a criminal offence before reaching the age of eighteen, the sentence for several criminal offences or under several judgments shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of Sections 50 and 51 of this Law, taking into account that the total term of deprivation of liberty for several criminal offences may not exceed twelve years and six months, and under several judgments — fifteen years.

(2)	Conditional early release from sentence may be initiated if the person has served not less than half of the imposed term of deprivation of liberty.

(3)	Conditional early release from sentence with the imposition of electronic monitoring may be initiated if the person has served not less than one third of the imposed term of deprivation of liberty.

(4)	A person who has committed a criminal violation or a less serious crime before reaching the age of eighteen shall be considered not convicted after serving the sentence.
(As worded by the Law of 17.12.2020, which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 68. Section. Coercive Measures of a Medical Nature

(1)	For persons who have committed the offences provided for in this Law but suffer from mental disorders and have been found to be non-imputable or of limited imputability, the following coercive measures of a medical nature may be imposed:

1)	outpatient treatment in a medical institution;

2)	treatment in a general-type psychiatric hospital (unit);

3)	treatment in a specialised psychiatric hospital (unit) with security.

(2)	If the person referred to in paragraph one of this Section, due to the nature of the offence committed and his or her mental state, is not dangerous to society, the court may place him or her in the care of relatives or other persons who provide care for the sick.

(3)	For the persons referred to in paragraph one of this Section who have been found to be of limited imputability, treatment may also be imposed in places of deprivation of liberty appropriate for them.
(As amended by the Law of 15.05.2014, which enters into force on 14.06.2014.)

Imposition of Compulsory Measures of a Medical Nature on Persons in a State of Insanity

(1)	The court may impose the compulsory measures of a medical nature provided for in this Law on persons who have committed the offences provided for in this Law while in a state of insanity, or who, after committing the offence or after the pronouncement of the judgment, have contracted a mental illness that has deprived them of the ability to understand their actions or to control them, if these persons, due to the nature of the offence committed and their mental state, are dangerous to society.

(2)	Compulsory treatment and the type of medical institution shall be determined by the court depending on the mental illness with which the person concerned has contracted and the nature of the offence committed by that person. When determining treatment in a psychiatric hospital (ward), the type thereof shall be chosen by the medical institution.

(3)	A person who, after committing a criminal offence or after the pronouncement of a judgment, has contracted a mental illness that has deprived him or her of the ability to understand his or her actions or to control them, may, upon recovery, be sentenced by the court if the limitation period has not expired or there is no other ground for his or her release from criminal liability and punishment.

(4)	The court shall terminate the application of a compulsory measure of a medical nature or change it to a less restrictive measure if the person concerned has recovered or his or her state of health has improved, or if it is established that the state of health of that person has otherwise changed to such an extent that he or she is no longer dangerous to society.

(41) The court may change a compulsory measure of a medical nature to a more restrictive measure if the person fails to comply with the compulsory measure of a medical nature imposed on him or her.

(5)	If such a person is sentenced to a punishment after recovery, the time during which compulsory measures of a medical nature have been applied shall be included in the term of the punishment.

## (Chapter 05

In the wording of the 2005 law, which enters into force on 01.10.2005.)

Article 70.1. Basis for the application of a coercive measure to a legal person

For a criminal offence provided for in the Special Part of this law, the court or, in cases provided for by law, the prosecutor may apply a coercive measure to a private law legal person, including a state or local government capital company, as well as to a partnership, if the offence has been committed in the interests of the legal person, for the benefit of this person or as a result of its inadequate supervision or control by a natural person acting individually or as a member of a collegial body of the respective legal person:

1) on the basis of the right to represent the legal person or act on its behalf;

2) on the basis of the right to make decisions in the name of the legal person;

3) exercising control within the legal person.
(In the wording of the law of 14.03.2013, which enters into force on 01.04.2013.)

Article 70.2. Types of coercive measures applicable to a legal person

(1) The following coercive measures may be imposed on a legal person:

1) liquidation;

2) restriction of rights;

3) confiscation of property;

4) pecuniary exaction.

(2) One or more of the coercive measures provided for in paragraph one of this Article may be applied to a legal person. When applying liquidation, other coercive measures shall not be imposed.

(3) The procedure for the execution of coercive measures shall be determined in accordance with law.

(4) For a criminal violation, less serious crime or serious crime provided for in the Special Part of this law, for which imprisonment of up to five years is provided, the prosecutor may impose a pecuniary exaction or restriction of rights on a legal person as a coercive measure by drawing up a directive on a coercive measure.
(In the wording of the law of 14.03.2013, with amendments made by the law of 10.03.2016, which enters into force on 07.04.2016.)

Article 70.3. Liquidation

(1) Liquidation is the compulsory termination of the activities of a legal person.

(2) A legal person shall be liquidated only in cases where the legal person has been specially created for the commission of a criminal offence or where a serious or particularly serious crime has been committed.

(3) Upon liquidation of a legal person, all property owned by it shall be expropriated without compensation into state ownership.
(With amendments made by the law of 14.03.2013, which enters into force on 01.04.2013.)

Article 70.4. Restriction of rights

(1) Restriction of rights is the withdrawal of certain rights or permits or the imposition of a prohibition that prevents a legal person from exercising certain rights, receiving state support or assistance, participating in state or local government procurement procedures, carrying out certain types of activities for a period from one year to ten years.

(2) (Deleted by the law of 10.03.2016)
(In the wording of the law of 14.03.2013, with amendments made by the law of 10.03.2016, which enters into force on 07.04.2016.)

Article 70.5. Confiscation of property

(1) Confiscation of property is the compulsory expropriation without compensation into state ownership of property owned by a legal person.

(2) The court, when imposing confiscation of property, shall specifically indicate which property is to be confiscated.

(3) (Deleted by the law of 14.03.2013)

(4) Property owned by a legal person that has been transferred to another person may also be confiscated.
(With amendments made by the laws of 13.12.2012 and 14.03.2013, which enters into force on 01.04.2013.)

Article 70.6. Pecuniary exaction

(1) A pecuniary exaction is a sum of money that the court or prosecutor orders to be paid to the state within 30 days in the amount specified in this Article.

(11) A pecuniary exaction, according to the harmfulness of the criminal offence and the financial situation of the legal person, shall be imposed:

1) for a criminal violation — in the amount of five to ten thousand minimum monthly wages established in the Republic of Latvia;

2) for a less serious crime — in the amount of ten to fifty thousand minimum monthly wages established in the Republic of Latvia;

3) for a serious crime — in the amount of twenty to seventy-five thousand minimum monthly wages established in the Republic of Latvia;

4) for a particularly serious crime — in the amount of thirty to one hundred thousand minimum monthly wages established in the Republic of Latvia.

(12) At the time of making the decision, the amount of the pecuniary exaction shall be indicated in the decision in the monetary units of the Republic of Latvia.

(2) A pecuniary exaction imposed on a legal person shall be paid from the funds of that person.

(3) The payment of the pecuniary exaction may be divided into instalments or postponed by the court or prosecutor respectively for a period not exceeding one year from the day when the decision or directive on the coercive measure has entered into legal force.

(4) If the pecuniary exaction is not paid, the coercive measure shall be executed by compulsory means.
(In the wording of the law of 14.03.2013, with amendments made by the laws of 29.10.2015 and 07.04.2022, which enters into force on 04.05.2022.)

Article 70.7. Compensation for harm
(Deleted by the law of 14.03.2013, which enters into force on 01.04.2013.)

Article 70.8. Conditions for the application of coercive measures to a legal person

(1) When determining the type of coercive measure, the nature of the criminal offence, the harm caused and whether a coercive measure has previously been applied to the legal person shall be taken into account.

(2) When determining the extent of the coercive measure, the following conditions shall be observed:

1) the actual conduct of the legal person;

2) the nature and consequences of the activities of the legal person;

3) measures taken by the legal person to prevent the commission of the criminal offence;

4) the size, type of occupation and financial situation of the legal person;

5) measures taken by the legal person to compensate for the loss caused or to eliminate the harm caused;

6) whether the legal person has reconciled with the victim.

(3) If several coercive measures have been applied to a legal person in accordance with paragraph two of Article 70.2 of this law, each of them shall be executed independently.

(4) In a criminal case concerning several independent criminal offences, the court, when making a judgment, or the prosecutor, when drawing up a directive on a coercive measure, shall impose a coercive measure on the legal person separately for each criminal offence. In such a case, the final set of coercive measures to be applied shall be determined according to the aggregate of criminal offences in the following order:

1) by subsuming the lighter pecuniary exaction into the more severe one or by adding them fully or partially;

2) by adding restrictions of rights fully;

3) by adding confiscations of property fully.

(5) If a legal person, after a judgment or prosecutor's directive on a coercive measure has entered into force but before the complete execution of the coercive measure, is involved in new criminal proceedings concerning the application of a coercive measure, the court shall add to the coercive measure imposed in the new judgment the coercive measure that has not been executed under the previous judgment or prosecutor's directive on a coercive measure, in the following order:

1) by adding pecuniary exactions fully or partially;

2) by adding restrictions of rights fully;

3) by adding confiscations of property fully.

(6) If liquidation has been applied, then in the cases referred to in paragraphs four and five of this Article, other coercive measures shall be subsumed into the liquidation.

(7) In the cases referred to in paragraphs four and five of this Article, the total amount or time of the coercive measure may exceed the maximum amount or time of the coercive measure provided for the most serious of the criminal offences committed, but not by more than half of the maximum amount or time of the coercive measure provided for the most serious of the criminal offences committed.
(In the wording of the law of 14.03.2013, with amendments made by the laws of 29.10.2015, 11.06.2020 and 07.04.2022, which enters into force on 04.05.2022.)

Article 70.9. Calculation of limitation period

(1) In proceedings concerning the application of a coercive measure, the limitation period shall be calculated from the day when the criminal offence was committed until the moment when the legal person is notified of the initiation of proceedings concerning the application of a coercive measure, observing the time limits specified in points 2 to 6 of paragraph one of Article 56 and in Article 57 of this law.

(2) A judgment or prosecutor's directive on the application of a coercive measure shall not be enforceable if five years have passed since the day it entered into legal force.
(In the wording of the law of 15.05.2014, which enters into force on 14.06.2014.)

## (Chapter 22

06.2017. law version, which enters into force 01.08.2017. See transitional provision point 21)

70.10 Article. Concept of special confiscation of property

Special confiscation of property is the compulsory uncompensated alienation into state ownership of criminally acquired property or an object of commission of a criminal offence, or property related to a criminal offence. Special confiscation of property is not a criminal punishment.
(22.06.2017. law version, which enters into force 01.08.2017.)

70.11 Article. Confiscation of criminally acquired property

(1)	Criminally acquired property is any economic benefit that has come into a person's ownership or possession directly or indirectly as a result of the commission of a criminal offence.

(11) Indirectly criminally acquired property is any economic benefit that has come into a person's ownership or possession directly as a result of further use of criminally acquired property, including as a result of reinvestment or transformation, or funds that a person has obtained from the realisation of such property, as well as fruits and profits obtained.

(2)	If the value of property is not commensurate with a person's lawful income and the person does not prove that the property was acquired lawfully, property that belongs to a person who:

1)	has committed a crime that by its nature is directed at obtaining material or other benefit, regardless of whether material or other benefit was obtained as a result of the crime;

2)	is a member of an organised group;

3)	has committed a crime related to terrorism,

may also be recognised as criminally acquired property.

(3)	Property that is in the possession of another such person who maintains permanent family, economic or other property relations with the person referred to in paragraph two of this Article may also be recognised as criminally acquired property, if the value of the property in this person's possession is not commensurate with their lawful income and if the person does not prove that the property was acquired lawfully.

(4)	Criminally acquired property shall be confiscated if it is not to be returned to the owner or lawful possessor.
(22.06.2017. law version with amendments made by 11.06.2020. and 07.04.2022. law, which enters into force 04.05.2022.)

70.12 Article. Confiscation of an object of commission of a criminal offence

(1)	An object of commission of a criminal offence is tools and means that were intended or used for the commission of a criminal offence.

(2)	Objects of commission of a criminal offence shall be confiscated.
(22.06.2017. law version, which enters into force 01.08.2017.)

70.13 Article. Confiscation of property related to a criminal offence

(1)	Property related to a criminal offence is items prohibited from circulation or items whose origin or ownership in the particular criminal case has not been established, or such property belonging to a person who has committed a criminal offence that

in connection with the criminal offence committed may not be left in the person's ownership.

(2)	Property related to a criminal offence shall be confiscated.

(3)	Animals may be confiscated if in connection with the criminal offence committed they may not be left in the ownership of a person who has committed a criminal offence.

(4)	A vehicle belonging to a person who has committed a criminal offence may be subject to confiscation if a criminal offence against traffic safety has been committed.

(5)	A vehicle belonging to a person who has committed a criminal offence, with which they have committed the criminal offence provided for in Article 262. or 262.1 of this law, shall be subject to confiscation.
(22.06.2017. law version with amendments made by 27.10.2022. law, which enters into force 25.11.2022.)

70.14 Article. Replacement of property to be confiscated

(1)	If an object of commission of a criminal offence belongs to another person, the value of the object of commission of a criminal offence may be recovered.

(11) If the criminal offence provided for in Article 262. or 262.1 of this law has been committed with a vehicle that belongs to another person, the full or partial value of this vehicle shall be recovered from the person who has committed the criminal offence.

(2)	If criminally acquired property has been alienated, destroyed, concealed or disguised and it is not possible to confiscate it, the value of the property to be confiscated may be recovered.

(3)	If confiscation of criminally acquired property has been applied to a person, the property to be confiscated may be replaced with financial means in the value of this property. Property that has historical, artistic or scientific value may not be replaced.

(4)	If it is not possible to confiscate criminally acquired property because it has been alienated, destroyed, concealed or disguised, and a person who has committed a criminal offence has no other property on which to direct recovery, the following may be confiscated:

1)	property that a person has alienated to another person after the commencement of a criminal offence without payment or for a value that is substantially lower or substantially higher than the market value;

2)	joint property of a person who has committed a criminal offence and their spouse, unless separation of spouses' property was established at least one year before the commencement of a criminal offence;

### 71.Article. Genocide

For genocide, that is, for intentional acts with the purpose of wholly or partially destroying any national, ethnic, racial or particular religious group of people as such, by killing members of such a group, inflicting bodily injuries dangerous to life or health upon them or bringing them to mental illness, intentionally creating living conditions for them that wholly or partially physically destroy these people, using means whose purpose is to prevent the birth of children in such a group, or forcibly transferring children from one group of people to another, —

the applicable sentence is life imprisonment or deprivation of liberty for a term of three to twenty years.
(With amendments made by 21.05.2009. law, which enters into force 01.07.2009.)

71.1 Article. Incitement to genocide

For public incitement to genocide —

the applicable sentence is deprivation of liberty for a term of up to eight years.
(28.04.2005. law version, which enters into force 01.06.2005.)

71.	2 Article. Crimes against humanity

For a crime against humanity, that is, for an act committed as part of a widespread or systematic attack against civilians and manifested as murder, extermination, enslavement, deportation or forced displacement, unlawful deprivation or restriction of liberty, torture, rape, involvement of a person in sexual slavery, coercion to engage in prostitution, forced impregnation or sterilisation or other sexual violence of similar severity, apartheid, persecution of any group of people or association based on political, racial, national, ethnic, cultural, religious or gender affiliation or other grounds recognised as inadmissible in international law, in connection with any act specified in this Article, or genocide, or a war crime, or other act provided for in international law binding on the Republic of Latvia that causes serious physical or mental suffering, —

the applicable sentence is life imprisonment or deprivation of liberty for a term of three to twenty years.
(21.05.2009. law version, which enters into force 01.07.2009.)

### 72. Article. Crimes against peace

For crimes committed against peace, that is, for planning, preparation, instigation of aggression, participation in it, for waging an aggressive war in violation of international treaties binding on the Republic of Latvia, for participation in a conspiracy with the purpose of committing the crimes referred to in this Article —

the applicable sentence is life imprisonment or deprivation of liberty for a term of three to twenty years.
(With amendments made by 16.10.2014. law, which enters into force 01.02.2015.)

04.2018. law version, which enters into force on 23.05.2018.)

79.1 Section. Terrorism

(1)	For explosions, arson, use of nuclear-chemical, chemical, biological, bacteriological, toxic or other weapons of mass destruction, mass poisoning, spreading of epidemics or epizootics, abduction of a person, hostage-taking, seizure of air, land or water transport, or other actions, if they are carried out with the intent to intimidate the population or to compel a state, its institutions or international organisations to perform any action or refrain from it, or to harm the interests of the state, its population or an international organisation (terrorism), —

punishable by life imprisonment or deprivation of liberty for a term from eight to twenty years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.

(2)	For destruction or damage of physical objects, automated data processing systems, electronic networks, as well as other objects located in the state territory or on the continental shelf, the purpose of which is to ensure state security, if such actions are carried out with the intent provided for in paragraph one of this Section, —

punishable by life imprisonment or deprivation of liberty for a term from ten to twenty years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.
(26.04.2018. law version, which enters into force on 23.05.2018.)

79.2 Section. Financing of Terrorism

(1)	For financing of terrorism —

punishable by life imprisonment or deprivation of liberty for a term from eight to twenty years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years or without it.

(2)	For financing of terrorism, if it is committed on a large scale, —

punishable by life imprisonment or deprivation of liberty for a term from ten to twenty years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years or without it.
(26.04.2018. law version, which enters into force on 23.05.2018.)

79.3 Section. Terrorist Group

(1)	For organising a terrorist group, that is, a group of persons by prior agreement, with the intent to commit one or more crimes related to terrorism, as well as for involvement in such a group —

punishable by deprivation of liberty for a term from eight to seventeen years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.

(2)	For leading a terrorist group or participating in the crimes referred to in paragraph one of this Section committed by such a group —

punishable by life imprisonment or deprivation of liberty for a term from twelve to twenty years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.
(26.04.2018. law version, which enters into force on 23.05.2018.)

79.4 Section. Recruitment, Training and Self-Training for Terrorism

(1)	For obtaining or receiving instructions, knowledge or practical skills with the intent to carry out or facilitate terrorism (self-training for terrorism) —

punishable by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to seven years and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.

(2)	For recruitment of a person for terrorism or involvement in a terrorist group or training for terrorism —

punishable by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to ten years and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.
(26.04.2018. law version, which enters into force on 23.05.2018.)

79.5 Section. Travelling for the Purpose of Terrorism

For travelling with the intent to carry out or facilitate terrorism, to join a terrorist group or to train or be trained for terrorism —

punishable by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to eight years and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.
(26.04.2018. law version, which enters into force on 23.05.2018.)

79.6 Section. Justification of Terrorism, Incitement to Terrorism and Terrorist Threats

(1)	For public glorification or justification of terrorism or for public incitement to terrorism, or for distribution of material glorifying, justifying or inciting terrorism —

punishable by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or short-term deprivation of liberty, or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.

(2)	For threats to carry out terrorism, if there is reason to believe that it may be carried out, —

punishable by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to eight years and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.
(26.04.2018. law version with amendments made by the law of 17.12.2020, which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

X	Chapter Crimes Against the State

### 80.Section. Activity Directed Against the Republic of Latvia

(1)	For activity directed against the state independence, sovereignty, territorial integrity, state power or state order of the Republic of Latvia in a manner not provided for in the Constitution of the Republic of Latvia, —

punishable by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to eight years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.

(2)	For the same activity, if it is committed using violence, or if it is committed by an organised group, or if it is committed by a state official or a responsible employee of an enterprise (company) or organisation, —

punishable by deprivation of liberty for a term from five to fifteen years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.
(21.04.2016. law version with amendments made by the law of 14.12.2023, which enters into force on 30.12.2023.)

80.1 Section. Association in an Organised Group with the Purpose of Carrying Out Activity Directed Against the Republic of Latvia

(1)	For association of more than two persons in an organised group with the intent to act against the state independence, sovereignty, territorial integrity, state power or state order of the Republic of Latvia in a manner not provided for in the Constitution of the Republic of Latvia —

punishable by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to eight years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.

(2)	For the same activity, if it is committed by a state official or a responsible employee of an enterprise (company) or organisation, —

punishable by deprivation of liberty for a term from two to ten years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.
(21.04.2016. law version with amendments made by the laws of 17.12.2020 and 14.12.2023, which enters into force on 30.12.2023.)

### 104. Section. Operation of Facilities Without Treatment Structures

For the operation of industrial, agricultural, municipal or other facilities if the necessary treatment, harmful substance and dust capture structures and devices have not been installed therein or they are in such a condition that they are not fit for operation, and if substantial harm has been caused thereby, —

shall be punished by short-term deprivation of liberty or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.
(In the wording of the Law of 21.10.2010 with amendments made by the Laws of 13.12.2012, 17.12.2020 and 07.04.2022, which come into force on 04.05.2022.)

104. 1 Section. Unlawful Operation of Installations

For unlawful operation of an installation specified in a pollution-regulating regulatory enactment in which environmentally hazardous activities are carried out or hazardous substances or preparations are stored or used, if substantial harm has been caused thereby,
—

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to two years or short-term deprivation of liberty, or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.
(In the wording of the Law of 25.09.2014 with amendments made by the Laws of 17.12.2020 and 07.04.2022, which come into force on 04.05.2022.)

### 105. Section. Failure to Take Measures to Eliminate Environmental Pollution

For failure to take or improper taking of measures necessary to eliminate environmental pollution and other harmful consequences falling within the duties of a person, as well as for failure to report if harmful consequences have occurred,
—

shall be punished by short-term deprivation of liberty or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 12.02.2004, 21.10.2010, 13.12.2012 and 17.12.2020, which come into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 106. Section. Concealment of Data on Environmental Pollution

(1) For failure to report pollution of sea waters or other harmful impact from vehicles or structures at sea, if committed by a person who had a duty to report, —

shall be punished by short-term deprivation of liberty or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.

(2) For intentional concealment or falsification of data on the extent of environmental pollution, if committed by a person who had a duty to provide such data, and if substantial harm has been caused as a result thereof, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to four years or short-term deprivation of liberty, or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.
(In the wording of the Law of 21.10.2010 with amendments made by the Laws of 13.12.2012, 17.12.2020 and 07.04.2022, which come into force on 04.05.2022.)

### 107. Section. Forest Burning

(1) For intentional setting fire to a forest —

shall be punished by short-term deprivation of liberty or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.

(2) For the same acts, if substantial harm has been caused thereby, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to three years or short-term deprivation of liberty, or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.

(3) For the same acts, if they have caused the death of a person or other serious consequences through the negligence of the guilty person,
—

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to eight years and probation supervision for a term of up to three years or without it.
(In the wording of the Law of 13.12.2012 with amendments made by the Law of 17.12.2020, which comes into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 108. Section. Destruction and Damage of Forest Through Negligence

(1) For destruction or damage of a forest area through negligence, by careless handling of fire or in another manner, if substantial harm has been caused thereby, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to two years or short-term deprivation of liberty, or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.

(2) For the same acts, if they have caused the death of a person or other serious consequences, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or short-term deprivation of liberty, or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 12.02.2004, 21.10.2010, 13.12.2012 and 17.12.2020, which come into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 109. Section. Unauthorised Felling and Damage of Trees

(1) For unauthorised felling of trees in another person's forest or other land area belonging to another person —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to two years or short-term deprivation of liberty, or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.

(2) For unauthorised felling, destruction or damage of trees in a specially protected nature area, micro-reserve, park, square, avenue or environmental and natural resource protection buffer zone —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to three years or short-term deprivation of liberty, or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.

(3) For unauthorised felling, destruction or damage of trees, if substantial harm has been caused by such acts, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or short-term deprivation of liberty, or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.

(4) For the criminal offence provided for in paragraph one, two or three of this Section, if committed by an organised group,
—

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to eight years.
(In the wording of the Law of 13.12.2007 with amendments made by the Laws of 21.10.2010, 13.12.2012, 29.10.2015, 08.06.2017 and
17.12.2020, which come into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 110. Section. Unauthorised Fishing and Acquisition of Aquatic Animals

(1) (Deleted by the Law of 21.10.2010)

(2) For catching or otherwise acquiring fish or aquatic animals without the relevant permit, at a prohibited time or in prohibited places, or with prohibited gear or methods (unauthorised acquisition), if substantial harm has been caused thereby, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to two years or short-term deprivation of liberty, or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.

(21) For the criminal offence provided for in paragraph two of this Section, if committed by a group of persons pursuant to prior agreement or if committed in a specially protected nature area, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to three years or short-term deprivation of liberty, or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.

(3) For unauthorised acquisition of fish or aquatic animals using electric current, explosive substances, poisonous substances or other generally dangerous means or methods, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to four years or short-term deprivation of liberty, or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 25.04.2002, 21.10.2010, 13.12.2012, 25.09.2014 and 17.12.2020, which
come into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 111. Section

Unlawful Manufacturing, Acquisition, Storage, Sale, Transportation and Forwarding of Electrofishing Devices

For unlawful manufacturing, acquisition, storage, sale, transportation or forwarding of electrofishing devices —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to two years or short-term deprivation of liberty, or probation supervision, or community service, or a fine.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 12.02.2004, 21.10.2010, 13.12.2012 and 17.12.2020, which come into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 123. Section. Manslaughter through Negligence

(1)	For unlawful manslaughter through negligence —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to three years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service.

(2)	For unlawful manslaughter through negligence, if two or more persons have been killed or if the manslaughter was committed while handling a firearm or explosives or in another generally dangerous manner, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service.
(With amendments made by the laws of 13.12.2012 and 17.12.2020, which enter into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 124. Section. Driving to Suicide

(1)	For driving a person to suicide or an attempt thereof, by treating the victim cruelly or systematically humiliating his or her personal dignity, if this person was not in material or other dependence on the guilty person, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to three years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service.
(2)	For the same acts in relation to a person who was in material or other dependence on the guilty person, — shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation
supervision, or by community service.
(With amendments made by the laws of 13.12.2012 and 17.12.2020, which enter into force on 01.01.2022.)

XIII	Chapter
Criminal Offences against the Health of a Person

### 125. Section. Intentional Grievous Bodily Harm

(1)	For intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to seven years and by probation supervision for a term of up to three years or without it.

(2)	For the same acts, if:

1)	they were committed in connection with the fact that the victim or his or her relative fulfilled his or her official or professional duties or participated in the prevention or interruption of a criminal or other unlawful act, or gave testimony in court or in pre-trial criminal proceedings;

2)	they were committed against two or more persons;

3)	they were committed in a manner dangerous to the life or health of several persons;

4)	they had the character of torture or torment;

5)	they were committed by a group of persons;

6)	(deleted by the law of 13.12.2012);

7)	they were committed by a person placed in a place of short-term detention or imprisonment;

8)	they were committed against a person in a helpless state;

9)	they were committed against a person with whom the perpetrator of the criminal offence is in the first or second degree of kinship, or against a spouse or former spouse, or against a person with whom the perpetrator of the criminal offence is or has been in a permanent intimate relationship, or against a person with whom the perpetrator of the criminal offence has a common (undivided) household, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term from two to ten years and by probation supervision for a term of up to three years or without it.

(3)	For infliction of intentional grievous bodily harm which, due to the negligence of the guilty person, has been the cause of the victim's death, or for infliction of intentional grievous bodily harm if it was committed by an organised group, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term from three to fifteen years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and by probation supervision for a term of up to three years or without it.

(4)	(Deleted by the law of 13.12.2012)
(With amendments made by the laws of 13.12.2007, 30.10.2008, 21.05.2009, 08.07.2011, 13.12.2012, 08.06.2017 and
26.04.2018, which enters into force on 23.05.2018.)

### 126. Section. Intentional Bodily Harm of Medium Gravity

(1)	For intentional infliction of bodily harm of medium gravity —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to three years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(2)	For the same acts, if:

1)	they were committed in connection with the fact that the victim or his or her relative fulfilled his or her official or professional duties or participated in the prevention or interruption of a criminal or other unlawful act, or gave testimony in court or in pre-trial criminal proceedings;

2)	they had the character of torture or torment;

3)	they were committed by a group of persons;

4)	(deleted by the law of 13.12.2012);

5)	they were committed by a person placed in a place of short-term detention or imprisonment;

6)	they were committed against a person in a helpless state;

7)	they were committed against a person with whom the perpetrator of the criminal offence is in the first or second degree of kinship,

or against a spouse or former spouse, or against a person with whom the perpetrator of the criminal offence is or has been in a permanent intimate relationship, or against a person with whom the perpetrator of the criminal offence has a common (undivided) household, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(With amendments made by the laws of 30.10.2008, 21.05.2009, 13.12.2012, 08.06.2017, 26.04.2018 and 17.12.2020,
which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 127. Section. Intentional Bodily Harm Inflicted in a State of Strong Mental Agitation

For intentional grievous or medium gravity bodily harm inflicted in a state of sudden strong mental agitation caused by violence or serious insult to honour from the victim, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to three years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(With amendments made by the laws of 13.12.2012 and 17.12.2020, which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 128. Section

Infliction of Intentional Bodily Harm by Exceeding the Limits of Necessary Defence

For infliction of intentional grievous or medium gravity bodily harm by exceeding the limits of necessary defence, if this harm was not inflicted while defending against a threat to life or against rape, —

shall be punished by short-term deprivation of liberty or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(With amendments made by the laws of 13.12.2012 and 17.12.2020, which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 129. Section

Infliction of Intentional Bodily Harm by Violating the Conditions of Detention of a Person

(1)	For infliction of intentional grievous or medium gravity bodily harm by violating the conditions of detention of a person, —

shall be punished by short-term deprivation of liberty or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(2)	For the same acts, if they were committed by a state official, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to one year or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2004, 13.12.2012 and 17.12.2020, which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 130. Section. Intentional Minor Bodily Injury

(1)	(Deleted by the Law of 21.10.2010.)

(2)	For intentional infliction of minor bodily injury, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to one year, or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(3)	For the same acts, if:

1)	they have been committed in connection with the victim or his or her relative having performed his or her official or professional duties or having participated in the prevention or interruption of a criminal or other unlawful act, or having given testimony in court or in pre-trial criminal proceedings;

2)	they have been of the nature of torture or torment;

3)	they have been committed by a group of persons;

4)	they have been committed by a person placed in a place of short-term detention or imprisonment;

5)	they have been committed against a person in a state of helplessness;

6)	they have been committed against a person with whom the perpetrator of the criminal offence is related in the first or second degree of kinship, or against a spouse or former spouse, or against a person with whom the perpetrator of the criminal offence is or has been in a permanent intimate relationship, or against a person with whom the perpetrator of the criminal offence has a joint (undivided) household, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to three years, or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 21.10.2010., 13.12.2012., 25.09.2014., 08.06.2017., 26.04.2018. and 17.12.2020.
which enter into force on 01.01.2022.)

130. Section 1. Torture

For torture, if these acts have not had the consequences provided for in Sections 125, 126 or 130 of this Law, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to one year, or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(In the wording of the Law of 25.09.2014. with amendments made by the Law of 17.12.2020., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 131. Section. Bodily Injury by Negligence

For infliction of serious or medium gravity bodily injury by negligence —

shall be punished by short-term deprivation of liberty or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 13.12.2012. and 17.12.2020., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 132. Section. Threats to Commit Murder and to Inflict Serious Bodily Injury

(1)	For threats to commit murder or to inflict serious bodily injury, if there has been reason to fear that these threats may be carried out, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to one year, or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(2)	For the same acts, if they have been committed against a person with whom the perpetrator of the criminal offence is related in the first or second degree of kinship, or against a spouse or former spouse, or against a person with whom the perpetrator of the criminal offence is or has been in a permanent intimate relationship, or against a person with whom the perpetrator of the criminal offence has a joint (undivided) household, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to three years, or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 13.12.2012., 17.12.2020. and 15.06.2023., which enters into force on 15.07.2023. See transitional provision point 25.1)

132.1 Section. Stalking

(1)	For repeated or prolonged stalking, surveillance, threatening or unwanted communication with another person, if that person has had reason to fear for his or her own safety or that of his or her relatives, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to one year, or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(2)	For the same acts, if they have been committed against a person with whom the perpetrator of the criminal offence is related in the first or second degree of kinship, or against a spouse or former spouse, or against a person with whom the perpetrator of the criminal offence

### 133.Section. Infection with Human Immunodeficiency and Hepatitis B and C Viruses

For deliberate infection of a person with human immunodeficiency virus or hepatitis B or C virus —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years, or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(In the wording of the Law of 21.05.2009. with amendments made by the Laws of 13.12.2012. and 17.12.2020., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

133. Section 1. Infection with a Dangerous Infectious Disease Agent

For deliberate infection of a person with a dangerous infectious disease agent, if it has resulted in serious consequences, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years, or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(In the wording of the Law of 21.05.2009. with amendments made by the Laws of 13.12.2012., 03.09.2020. and 17.12.2020., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 134. Section. Infection with a Sexually Transmitted Disease Agent

(1)	For deliberate infection of a person with a sexually transmitted disease agent —

shall be punished by short-term deprivation of liberty or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(2)	For deliberate infection of a minor with a sexually transmitted disease agent —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to one year, or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 12.02.2004., 21.05.2009., 13.12.2012. and 17.12.2020., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 135. Section. Unlawful Performance of Abortion

(1)	For an abortion performed on a pregnant woman by a person who has the right to do so, if the abortion has been performed outside a hospital or other medical institution or in a medical institution but without legal basis, —

shall be punished by short-term deprivation of liberty or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine, with deprivation of the right to engage in medical practice for a term of up to five years.

(2)	For performance of an abortion on a pregnant woman in unsanitary conditions or if it has been performed by a person who does not have the right to perform an abortion,—

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to two years, or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine, with deprivation of the right to engage in medical practice for a term of up to five years.

(3)	(Deleted by the Law of 13.12.2012.)

(4)	For unlawful performance of an abortion against the will of the pregnant woman or if the unlawful performance of an abortion has caused the death of the pregnant woman or other serious consequences —

(With amendments made by the Laws of 12.02.2004., 13.12.2012. and 17.12.2020., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 136. Section. Coercion to Have an Abortion

For coercion of a pregnant woman to have an abortion, if as a result the abortion has been performed, —

shall be punished by short-term deprivation of liberty or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 13.12.2012. and 17.12.2020., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 137. Section. Unlawful Medical Practice

(1)	For unlawful medical practice, if it has caused a health disorder to the victim, —

shall be punished by short-term deprivation of liberty or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(2)	For unlawful medical practice, if it has caused the death of the victim or serious bodily injury through the negligence of the guilty person,
—

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to eight years.
(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2004., 13.12.2012. and 17.12.2020., which enter into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 138. Section. Improper Performance of Professional Duties by a Medical Practitioner

(1)	For the non-performance of professional duties by a medical practitioner or for negligent performance thereof, if this act has caused serious or moderate bodily injury to the victim through the negligence of the guilty person, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to one year or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(2)	For the same act, if it has caused the infection of the victim with human immunodeficiency virus or hepatitis B or C virus, or has been the cause of the death of the victim, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2004., 21.05.2009., 13.12.2012. and 17.12.2020., which enter into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 139. Section. Unlawful Removal and Use of Human Tissues and Organs

(1)	For unlawful removal or use of tissues or organs of a deceased person for medical or any other purposes —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to three years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(2)	For unlawful removal or use of tissues or organs of a living person for medical or any other purposes —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(3)	For the acts provided for in the first or second paragraph of this Section, if they have been committed with mercenary intent or if they have been committed by a group of persons, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to seven years.

(4)	For the acts provided for in the first or second paragraph of this Section, if they have been committed by a medical practitioner or if they have been committed by an organised group, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to ten years, with deprivation of the right to engage in medical practice for a term of up to five years.
(In the wording of the law of 13.12.2012. with amendments made by the laws of 06.06.2019., 17.12.2020. and 06.07.2021., which enter into force on 05.08.2021. The amendment in the first paragraph replacing the words "forced labour" with the words "probation supervision, or by community service" enters into force on 01.01.2022. The amendment in the second paragraph replacing the words "or by forced labour" with the words "or by probation supervision, or by community service" enters into force on 01.01.2022. See transitional provision point 26)

139.	1 Section. Recruitment of Donors and Recipients of Human Tissues and Organs
(1)	For recruitment of a donor or recipient for unlawful removal or transplantation of human tissues or organs — shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to one year or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation
supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(2)	For the same acts, if they have been committed with mercenary intent or if they have been committed by a group of persons, or if they have been committed by a medical practitioner, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to two years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(In the wording of the law of 06.06.2019. with amendments made by the law of 06.07.2021., which enters into force on 05.08.2021. The amendments in the first and second paragraphs replacing the words "or by forced labour" with the words "or by probation supervision, or by community service" enter into force on 01.01.2022. See transitional provision point 26)

### 140. Section. Violation of Sanitary-Hygienic and Epidemiological Safety Regulations

For violation of sanitary-hygienic or epidemiological safety regulations, if it has caused an epidemic or other serious consequences, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2004., 13.12.2012., 03.09.2020. and 17.12.2020., which enter into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 141. Section. Abandonment Without Assistance

(1)	For failure to provide necessary and obviously urgent assistance to a person who is in a life-threatening condition, if the guilty person was aware that he or she could provide it without serious danger to himself or herself and other persons, and if the failure to provide assistance has caused the death of a person or other serious consequences,—

shall be punished by probation supervision or by community service or by a fine.

(2)	For deliberate abandonment without assistance of a person who is in a condition dangerous to life or health and who has no possibility to preserve himself or herself due to minority, age, illness or his or her incapacity, if the guilty person had the possibility to provide assistance to the victim and had a duty to care for him or her or the guilty person himself or herself placed him or her in a life-threatening condition, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to two years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(21) For the acts provided for in the second paragraph of this Section, if the failure to provide assistance has caused the death of a person or other serious consequences, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to four years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation

supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(3)	For the acts provided for in the first or second paragraph of this Section, if the failure to provide assistance has caused the death of two or more persons, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(With amendments made by the laws of 13.12.2012., 25.09.2014., 07.01.2021. and 17.12.2020. and 06.07.2021., which enter into force on 05.08.2021. The amendment in paragraph 2.1 replacing the words "or by forced labour" with the words "or by probation supervision, or by community service" enters into force on 01.01.2022. See transitional provision point 26)

### 142. Section. Failure to Provide Assistance to Victims at Sea

(1)	For failure to proceed to the scene of a disaster at sea, if a message has been received that assistance is necessary, and if committed by a ship's captain, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to two years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(2)	For failure to provide assistance to persons who are perishing at sea or on another waterway, if this assistance could be provided without serious danger to the ship, its crew and passengers and if committed by a ship's captain, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(In the wording of the law of 13.12.2012. with amendments made by the law of 17.12.2020., which enter into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 152. Section. Unlawful Deprivation of Liberty

(1)	For unlawful actions depriving a person of the possibility to freely determine their location (unlawful deprivation of liberty), if there are no elements of a criminal offence by a State official, —

shall be punished by short-term deprivation of liberty or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(2)	For the same actions, if they have been committed in a manner dangerous to the victim's life or health or if they are associated with infliction of physical suffering on them, or if they have lasted more than one week, or if they have been committed by a group of persons pursuant to prior agreement, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to three years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(3)	For unlawful deprivation of liberty, if it has caused serious consequences or if it has been committed by an organised group, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to seven years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years or without it.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 12.02.2004., 13.12.2007., 08.07.2011., 13.12.2012. and 17.12.2020., which
come into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 153. Section. Abduction of a Person

(1)	For seizure of a person using violence or threats, or taking away by deceit or by exploiting the person's state of helplessness (abduction of a person), —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(2)	For the same actions, if they have been committed against a minor, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to seven years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.

(3)	For abduction of a person, if it has caused serious consequences or it has been committed against an infant, or it has been committed by an organised group, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term from three to twelve years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years or without it.

(With amendments made by the Laws of 13.12.2007., 30.10.2008., 08.07.2011., 13.12.2012. and 17.12.2020., which
come into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 154. Section. Seizure of Hostages

(1)	For seizure or detention of a person as a hostage, if it is associated with threats to kill, inflict bodily injuries or continue to detain this person with the aim of compelling a natural or legal person or a group of persons to perform any action or refrain from it, putting forward this as a condition for the release of the hostage, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term from two to ten years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years or without it.

(2)	For the same actions, if they have been committed against a minor or if they have been committed by a group of persons pursuant to prior agreement, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term from three to twelve years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.

(3)	For the actions provided for in paragraph one of this Section, if they have caused serious consequences or if they have been committed against an infant, or if they have been committed by an organised group, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term from five to fifteen years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.

154.1 Section. Trafficking in Human Beings

(1)	For trafficking in human beings —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to eight years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property.

(2)	For trafficking in human beings, if it has been committed against a minor or if it has been committed by a group of persons pursuant to prior agreement, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term from three to twelve years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years or without it.

(3)	For trafficking in human beings, if it has endangered the victim's life or caused serious consequences or if it has been committed with particular cruelty or against an infant, or if it has been committed by an organised group, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term from five to fifteen years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years or without it.
(As worded by the Law of 25.04.2002. with amendments made by the Laws of 16.12.2004., 13.12.2007., 08.07.2011., 13.12.2012. and 14.03.2013., which comes into force on 01.04.2013. See transitional provision paragraph 11)

154.	2 Section. Concept of Trafficking in Human Beings

(1)	Trafficking in human beings is the recruitment, transportation, transfer, harbouring, accommodation or receipt of persons for the purpose of exploitation, using violence or threats, or taking away by deceit or by exploiting the person's dependence on the guilty party or their vulnerability or state of helplessness, or by giving or receiving material or other benefits in order to obtain the consent to trafficking of the person on whom the victim is dependent.

(2)	The recruitment, transportation, transfer, harbouring, accommodation or receipt of a minor for the purpose of exploitation shall be recognised as trafficking in human beings even if it is not associated with the use of any of the means referred to in paragraph one of this Section.

(3)	Exploitation within the meaning of this Section is the involvement of a person in prostitution or other forms of sexual exploitation, coercion to perform work, provide services or commit criminal offences, keeping in slavery or other forms similar to it (debt bondage, serfdom or other forms of forced transfer of a person into dependence on another person), keeping in servitude or unlawful removal of a person's tissues or organs.

(4)	State of vulnerability within the meaning of this Section means that circumstances are exploited where the person has no other real or acceptable choice but to submit to exploitation.
(As worded by the Law of 25.04.2002. with amendments made by the Laws of 13.12.2012. and 25.09.2014., which comes into force on 29.10.2014.)

### 176. Section. Robbery

(1)	For the seizure of another's movable property, if it is connected with violence or the threat of violence (robbery), —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property.

(2)	For robbery, if it has been committed in a substantial amount or if it has been committed by a group of persons pursuant to prior agreement, or if it has been committed by entering a vehicle, dwelling or other premises, or if it has been committed from a storage facility or a device connecting storage facilities, as well as for the robbery of a vehicle —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to eight years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.

(3)	For robbery, if it has been committed in a large amount or if it has been committed by an organised group, as well as for the robbery of narcotic, psychotropic, potent, toxic or radioactive substances, explosives, firearms or ammunition —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of three to twelve years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.

(4)	For robbery, if it has been committed using firearms or explosives, or if it is connected with the infliction of serious bodily injury on the victim, or if it has caused other serious consequences, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of five to fifteen years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years.
(With amendments made by the laws of 25.04.2002., 12.02.2004., 08.07.2011., 13.12.2012., 06.06.2019. and 17.12.2020.
which enter into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 177. Section. Fraud

(1)	For the acquisition of another's property or rights to such property by abusing trust or by deceit (fraud), —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to three years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(2)	For fraud, if it has been committed in a substantial amount or if it has been committed by a group of persons pursuant to prior agreement,
—

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property.

(3)	For fraud, if it has been committed in a large amount or if it has been committed by an organised group, or if it has been committed by acquiring narcotic, psychotropic, potent, toxic or radioactive substances, explosives, firearms or ammunition,
—

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of two to ten years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years or without it.
(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2004., 13.12.2007., 08.07.2011., 13.12.2012., 17.12.2020. and 07.04.2022.
which enter into force on 04.05.2022.)

177. 1 Section. Fraud in an automated data processing system

(1)	For the acquisition of another's property or rights to such property, or other material benefits, by deliberately entering false data into an automated data processing system in order to influence the operation of its resources (computer fraud), —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to three years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(2)	For computer fraud, if it has been committed by a group of persons pursuant to prior agreement, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property.

(3)	For computer fraud, if it has been committed in a large amount or if it has been committed by an organised group, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of two to ten years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years or without it.
(In the wording of the law of 28.04.2005. with amendments made by the laws of 13.12.2007., 08.07.2011., 13.12.2012. and 17.12.2020. which enter into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 178. Section. Insurance fraud

(1)	For the intentional destruction, damage or concealment of one's own property with the intent to receive insurance compensation —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to two years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(2)	For coercing or persuading another person to destroy, damage or conceal insured property or other influence with the same purpose, if it has been committed by the owner of the property with the intent to receive the insurance sum, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to three years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.

(3)	For the acts provided for in the first or second paragraph of this Section, if they have been committed with the intent to receive the insurance sum in a large amount, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2004., 13.12.2012. and 17.12.2020. which enter into force on 01.01.2022.)

### 179. Section. Misappropriation

(1)	For the unlawful acquisition or squandering of another's property, if it has been committed by a person to whom this property was entrusted or in whose possession it was (misappropriation), —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to two years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property.

(2)	For misappropriation, if it has been committed in a substantial amount or if it has been committed by a group of persons pursuant to prior agreement, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to five years or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property.

(3)	For misappropriation, if it has been committed in a large amount, as well as for the misappropriation of narcotic, psychotropic, potent, toxic or radioactive substances, explosives, firearms or ammunition —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to ten years, with confiscation of property or without confiscation of property, and with probation supervision for a term of up to three years or without it.
(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2004., 13.12.2012., 17.12.2020. and 07.04.2022. which enter into force on 04.05.2022.)

### 180. Section. Theft, fraud, misappropriation in a minor amount

(1)	For theft, fraud or misappropriation in a minor amount, except for the offences provided for in the third and fourth paragraphs of Section 175, the third paragraph of Section 177 and the third paragraph of Section 179 of this law, —

shall be punished by deprivation of liberty for a term of up to one year or by short-term deprivation of liberty, or by probation supervision, or by community service, or by a fine.
